metros.name: Toronto
metros.regulationNote: We could not verify this city’s municipal rules for second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers from an official source, so we state none. Check with the City or the province before relying on anything you read about them elsewhere.

orgs.name: Sonic Boom Records
buys: Vinyl LPs across Rock, Pop, Soul, R&B, Blues, Jazz, Reggae, International, Punk, Metal, Psychedelic, Garage Rock, Hip Hop, Electronic, Country, Folk and Soundtracks
Inherited and collector record collections of any size
refuses: Classical, Vocal, Easy Listening and Religious records are rarely bought
orgs.dealNote: Counter purchase, with a buyer on duty 11am to 8pm, 364 days a year. They buy from a few LPs up to a whole collection and state most purchases take 30 minutes or less, longer at busy times or for large collections. Records brought in after 7pm are processed the next business day; you can also leave them for evaluation and a callback within 48 hours. They state they "will happily travel to take a look at larger collections of greater value". Every record is condition-checked individually.
orgs.locationsNote: One store on Spadina in Chinatown. Buying counter 11am-8pm daily; email shop@sonicboommusic.com.
orgs.caution: Their site states "Government issued photo ID is required by law when selling used product to Sonic Boom" — turning up without it ends the trip. If the collection is mostly Classical, Vocal, Easy Listening or Religious, call first; they rarely buy those genres and you would otherwise carry the boxes both ways. They travel only for larger collections of greater value, so do not assume a house call for a few crates.

orgs.name: Standard Auto Wreckers
buys: Junk, wrecked, old and non-running cars
orgs.dealNote: Submit a form or phone for a "no-obligation cash offer" on the vehicle; the page promises a "fair cash offer" whether or not the car runs. Free junk car removal and free towing across the Greater Toronto Area, so the vehicle does not need to be driveable. A licensed auto recycler, serving the GTA since 1979. The page states "No need to worry about towing or paperwork — our team handles everything", but it does NOT say what documents or identification you must produce, how payment is made, or when it is handed over.
orgs.locationsNote: Scarborough yard, with towing across Scarborough, North York, East York, York, Toronto and surrounding Ontario cities.
orgs.caution: Three things are absent from the page and should be settled on the phone before a truck is dispatched: what documents and identification you need, whether payment is cash, cheque or transfer, and at what point it is handed over. You are transferring a titled asset, so do not let the vehicle leave on a verbal assurance. The offer is also made before anyone has seen the car — confirm whether it is the price on collection or an opening figure.

orgs.name: VSP Consignment
buys: Authenticated luxury and contemporary designer fashion
Named top-selling brands including Gucci, Hermès, Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Prada, Dior, Bottega Veneta and Saint Laurent
orgs.dealNote: Consignment of authenticated designer fashion, so payment follows a sale rather than arriving at the counter. No appointment is needed — "You don't need to make an appointment to meet with one of our luxury specialists." Specialists will travel within the Greater Toronto Area and Calgary to advise on a wardrobe, which is worth asking about if you are clearing one. On payment the site says only: "Please call or email the location where you consigned your goods, and we will issue you a cheque for the next payment cycle." The payout percentage, minimum item value, consignment period and markdown schedule are NOT published anywhere on their site and are deliberately left blank here.
orgs.singleAddress: 1410 Dundas St. W, Toronto, ON M6J 1Y5
orgs.locationsNote: Toronto store on Dundas West; a second location in Calgary at 8244 Elbow Drive SW. Toronto enquiries: info@vspconsignment.com.

orgs.name: Around The Block
buys: Tableware, silver plate and sterling silver
refuses: Coach, Michael Kors, Tory Burch and Kate Spade handbags
orgs.dealNote: Consignment with a flat published split: "You will receive 60% of the sale price of your items", the shop retaining 40%. Pricing holds for the first 60 days, then the item is "reduced by 10% of the original price" and continues to reduce by 10% of the initial price every 30 days until it sells; gold and silver reduce by 5% on the same schedule. Unusually, there is no expiry — "Unless your items are seasonal, we are happy to keep your items until they sell! There is no expiration date." Cheques over $20 are mailed to consignors in the first week of each month for the previous month's sales; amounts under $20 are held and batched. No house visits for ordinary consignments — you deliver. For estates or large volumes they ask for JPEG photos of the rooms and decide case by case.
orgs.locationsNote: Showroom on Lesmill Road in the Don Mills area of North York. Their consignment page states Tuesday to Saturday, 11am-4pm, by appointment only — do not arrive unannounced. Email unique@aroundtheblock.com about large items.
orgs.caution: The refusal list is long and specific: no clothing, no appliances, no mattresses, no flat-pack furniture, no entertainment units, and four named handbag brands turned away. Check it before loading a van, and book — the showroom is appointment-only. "No expiration date" also means an unsold piece can sit indefinitely while the 10%-per-month ladder keeps eroding the price your 60% is calculated on.

orgs.name: BMV Books
buys: Books — fiction, non-fiction, recent releases and classics
Comics, pre-1990s or very new, and timeless classics
Antiquarian books, first editions and signed books
Vinyl LPs and some 45s, and select CDs
DVDs and Blu-rays — sci-fi, horror, Criterion, Kino, classic TV
Music, film, fashion and vintage magazines
Board games and action figures, complete and in original packaging, at the Bloor Street store only
refuses: Books in poor condition — water damage, cracked spines, yellowed pages
Outdated reference books on computers, travel, health and politics
Hardcover pop fiction already available in paperback
orgs.dealNote: Straightforward counter purchase: bring items to the buying counter at any of the three stores, they make an offer on what they can resell, and you "Take the Cash" on the spot. Anything declined you can donate to them or take home. "No appointment is necessary, but we strongly recommend you call ahead if you have more than two boxes of material." They will look at anything from a single item to a full library. No ID requirement is stated on their site.
orgs.locationsNote: Three stores: Annex, 471 Bloor St. West (416-967-5757); Uptown, 2289 Yonge Street (416-482-6002); Downtown, 10 Edward Street (416-977-3087). Board games and action figures are bought at the Bloor Street store only.
orgs.caution: No house calls are mentioned, so a large library means several car trips — call ahead if you have more than two boxes rather than arriving with a full trunk. Condition decides everything: cracked spines, yellowed pages and water damage are refused, as are encyclopedias, old atlases and dated reference books, which is a large share of what comes out of a cleared house. Expect to donate or re-load some of what you bring.

orgs.name: Canada Gold (Toronto Gold)
buys: Gold, silver and platinum bullion — bars, ingots, rounds and coins
Luxury watches — Rolex, Omega, Tudor, Cartier, Breitling, Patek Philippe, IWC, Audemars Piguet
Natural diamonds, colour N or better and over 0.4 carats
Old Canadian paper money and rare bills
orgs.dealNote: Outright purchase against published prices, which is the exception in this category. The site publishes a buy-price table in Canadian dollars per gram by purity — 24kt, 22kt, 21kt, 18kt, 14kt, 10kt and 9kt — and states "Our pricing is based on a percentage of the spot price and updates throughout the day". It does not state what that percentage is, so none is given here. No appointment needed: "visit our Bloorcourt location at 829 Bloor Street West - no appointment needed." Valuations are done on site in front of you. The site states a valid government-issued photo ID "is required by law to complete any transaction" and that you must be 18 or older.
orgs.locationsNote: Bloorcourt store on Bloor West. Mon-Fri 10:00am-6:00pm, Sat 10:00am-5:00pm, closed Sunday.
orgs.caution: They publish the method (a percentage of spot) but not the percentage, so the per-gram table is the number to check — look it up the morning you go, since they say it moves during the day. Scrap purchases are priced by weight and purity, so a piece with separate value as jewellery, as an antique, or by its maker is worth pricing on that basis first; melting cannot be undone. Photo ID and 18+ are required.

orgs.name: Canada Iron & Metal
buys: Computers, televisions, keyboards and circuit boards
orgs.dealNote: A working scrap yard that states "We buy metal from the general public" and has an "OPEN TO THE PUBLIC" section. You bring material in, it is weighed and graded, and you are paid against the day's market for that grade. Appliances, copper, brass, aluminum and end-of-life electronics from a house clearance are all on their accepted list. They also run bins for demolition and industry; residential pickup is not advertised. No prices, no payment method and no ID requirement are published on their site.
orgs.singleAddress: 3534 Dundas St W, York, ON M6S 2S1
orgs.locationsNote: NE corner of Jane and Dundas West in the Junction, convenient to west Toronto and Etobicoke. Mon-Fri 7:30am-5:00pm, Sat 7:30am-12:30pm. Email info@canadairon.com.
orgs.caution: Scrap has no fixed price and this yard publishes none — the figure depends on weight, grade and how well the material is separated, so the only real quote is the one at the scale. Separating copper from steel before you go changes the number. Their site says nothing about identification or payment method, so call ahead if either matters to you, and bring photo ID in case.

orgs.name: Common Sort
buys: Gently used fashionable clothing, men's and women's
refuses: Items that are not clean, not in good condition, off-trend or out of season
More than three grocery-store-sized bags per visit
Sellers under 18 or without valid ID
orgs.dealNote: Buys outright — not consignment — and, rare in this market, publishes the rate: 50% of the price they will sell the item for in store credit, or 25% of that same price in cash. Valid ID is required and you must be 18 or over. No appointment: you drop items off with your name and cell number, a buyer reviews them and texts you when finished. Anything declined must be collected the same day — items left more than 24 hours are considered abandoned. Buying counters take drop-offs daily from 11am until two hours before closing, with pickup at least an hour before closing.
orgs.locationsNote: Only 527 Bloor Street West (the Annex) could be confirmed on their own site in this pass, and no phone number is published there. Other Toronto and Montreal locations are referred to elsewhere but were not verified — check their site before travelling to any other address.
orgs.caution: Read the number carefully: 25% cash is 25% of the price THEY will sell it for, not of what you paid. An item they will retail at $80 pays $20 cash or $40 in credit. Store credit is only worth the extra if you will actually spend it. Three bags maximum per visit, bring ID, and collect anything they decline the same day or it is treated as abandoned.

orgs.name: Device Mart
buys: Apple, Samsung, Dell and MSI devices
Devices in any condition, including damaged
orgs.dealNote: Outright purchase of used electronics, with three routes: walk into a store, have them collect, or use a free prepaid shipping label. Payment timing is published: "Payment for devices picked up will be made immediatley upon collection", while "For devices shipped to us, payment will be processed and issued within 2 business days upon receipt and inspection of the device." They state they "pay top dollar for many types of electronics, even broken" and accept devices "in any condition", so a cracked or dead unit is still worth a quote. A pick-up service is offered for clients in Toronto. There is also a trade-in-for-credit option, separate from the cash purchase — make clear which you want. No ID requirement is stated on the site.
orgs.locationsNote: Two GTA stores: Scarborough, Unit 2, 1415 Kennedy Rd, M1P 2L6 (647-781-7355); and Downtown Toronto, Unit 11, 384 Yonge St, M5G 2K2 (647-557-5544).
orgs.caution: Sign out of your accounts and wipe the device before handing it over. On Apple hardware, leaving Activation Lock enabled means the buyer cannot resell it; their site does not state how they handle that, so clear it first rather than finding out at the counter. Their online estimator is an estimate — the binding number comes after physical inspection, since condition drives it. Note that they offer both a cash purchase and a trade-in credit; confirm which you are being quoted.

orgs.name: Dundas West Pawnbrokers / The Pawnshop (Toronto Pawn)
buys: Gold jewellery, precious gems and gold coins
orgs.dealNote: The clearest published pawn terms found in Toronto. PAWN LOAN: the site states "Interest is 2% per month simple interest"; the loan "is redeemed by payment of principle, plus interest & applicable service charges on or before the one year anniversary date", and "may be renewed by payment of interest & applicable service charges" by the same date. It states "We do not have a maximum cash limit for loans". ID rule is explicit: "Government ID required, other than Health Card". OUTRIGHT PURCHASE: the same page states they "purchase and make collateral loans on" gold jewellery, precious gems, luxury watches and gold coins — both transactions on the same goods.
orgs.locationsNote: Two shops: Dundas West Pawnbrokers, 2951 Dundas Street West, Toronto ON M6P 1Z2 (416-767-5833); and The Pawnshop, 1814 Danforth Avenue, Toronto ON M4C 1H8 (416-465-1968). Mon-Fri 10am-7pm, Sat 10am-6pm, closed Sundays and holidays.
orgs.caution: 2% per month is a monthly rate, not an annual one — carried simple over the full twelve-month term that is 24% of the principal in interest, before any service charges on a renewal. If the ticket is not redeemed by the anniversary date the item is forfeited. A health card will be turned away at the counter; bring a driver's licence or passport.

orgs.name: GUFF
buys: Vintage teak, rosewood, walnut and oak pieces
orgs.dealNote: Buys outright, and makes the distinction explicitly on their own page: "Whereas most stores operate on a consignment basis, here at Guff we outright buy." You are paid without waiting for the item to sell and without collecting anything unsold. The process is remote-first: fill in the form on their site with your contact details, a description and photographs, and "if there's interest we will arrange a time to meet" to look at what you are selling. That makes it a low-effort first call for a house clearance — you find out whether anything is worth money before moving furniture.
orgs.locationsNote: Store near Leslieville. Mon-Sat 11am-5pm, Sun 11am-3pm.
orgs.caution: They are specialists rather than a general clearance service — the demand is for mid-century Scandinavian, teak, rosewood, walnut and oak, vintage lighting and designer pieces, so ordinary modern or flat-pack furniture is unlikely to be taken. Their page does not say whether they collect from the home, so establish that at the viewing before planning the rest of the clear-out around it. No price guidance is published; the offer follows the viewing.

orgs.name: McTamney's
orgs.dealNote: Two different transactions, and the site treats them separately. PAWN LOAN: a collateral loan on contracts "that are good for up to 1 year", with "No duration minimums, no early payment penalties." The site publishes its cost of borrowing — "48% APR on all loan principals below $999" and "35% APR on all loan principals above $1000" — and gives worked examples of $20 interest per month on a $500 loan and $0.95 interest per day on a $1,000 loan. On default the site states "the item(s) will be put out for sale". To redeem you bring your ticket and a copy of your government-issued ID. OUTRIGHT SALE: there is a separate Sell page and the site states "we take gold, jewellery, guitars, cameras, cellphones and more", but publishes no purchase terms. Ask for the purchase price and the loan offer as two separate numbers.
orgs.locationsNote: One location on the Danforth. Mon-Fri 9:30am-5:30pm, Sat 9:30am-5pm, closed Sunday.
orgs.caution: Pawning is borrowing, not selling: if the contract defaults the item is put out for sale and you do not get it back. Use the shop's own published example to see the cost — they state $20 interest per month on a $500 loan. Government-issued ID is needed and the site states health cards are not accepted.

orgs.name: Of Things Past
refuses: Anything not showroom-ready — items must be clean and polished, without odour, damage, rips, fading or staining, and fully and properly assembled
orgs.dealNote: Consignment, so you are paid only after the item sells. Published split by final selling price: $5,001 and up, consignor 60% / shop 40%; $51 to $5,000, a 50/50 split; $50 or less, consignor 45% / shop 55%. Term is a "minimum of 150 days and a maximum of 180 days". Prices reduce on a published ladder — 10% at day 31, 20% at day 61, 30% at day 91, 40% at day 121. From day 151 to 180 unsold items may be reclaimed free of charge. From day 181 the shop owns anything unsold. Cheques are mailed by the 15th of the month following the sale once the account reaches a $100 minimum, with a $5 fee per cheque and a $35 fee to reissue one.
orgs.locationsNote: One showroom in North York. Open seven days a week, 10am-6pm.
orgs.caution: Three terms cost real money. Retrieving an item before day 151 triggers an early termination fee of 20% of the initial selling price. Nothing pays out until your account reaches $100, and each cheque costs $5. And an item that sells at day 121 sells at 40% off its original ticket, so your percentage is taken on the reduced figure, not the price it was first listed at. If you leave it past day 180 the shop owns it.

orgs.name: Pawn Kings
buys: Jewellery — rings, chains, necklaces, earrings, watches
Electronics — TVs, game consoles, laptops, cameras
Collectibles — box sets, action figures, coins, cards, comic books
orgs.dealNote: Their site asks you to "Simply decide if your looking to sell your item or do a buy-back" — an outright sale, or an arrangement under which you get the item back. NOTHING about the buy-back side is published: no interest rate, no term, no fee, no statement of what happens if you do not return. No ID requirement is published either. The value of this entry is geographic — it is the Brampton option.
orgs.locationsNote: Brampton: 73 Main Street N (905-497-7296). Hamilton: 501 Main St E (289-389-0757). The site claims "We have multiple location across the GTA" but lists no Toronto address and no third location.
orgs.caution: A "buy-back" is not the same as a sale — you are getting the item back only on terms the site does not publish anywhere. Before agreeing to one, ask for the cost, the deadline and what happens on default, in writing. The homepage claims GTA locations it does not list, so confirm the branch and its hours before travelling.

orgs.name: PayMore
buys: PlayStation, Xbox and Nintendo Switch consoles
Cameras, headphones, smartwatches and audio equipment
refuses: Items with no resale value — the site states they "can only pay for items that have resale value"
orgs.dealNote: A storefront buyer, not a mail-in service: bring the device in, they evaluate it, and the site states "If you accept, you'll receive immediate payment in cash – no waiting periods or delayed transactions." You are told to bring "your valid ID". Damaged devices are considered, with condition affecting the valuation. No pickup or collection service is mentioned.
orgs.locationsNote: NO store inside Toronto. Brampton: 380 Bovaird Drive East, L6Z 2S1, (289) 948-1810. Kitchener: 945 Victoria Street North, N2B 3C6, (226) 812-1333. Hamilton and Oakville are listed as coming soon.
orgs.caution: Despite appearing under a Toronto heading, the nearest branch is Brampton — check the map before driving out from the city centre or the east end. Factory-reset and sign out of every device first; an account still signed in usually means the device cannot be resold. Bring valid photo ID, which they ask for.

orgs.name: Queenglad Pawnbrokers
orgs.dealNote: Buys, sells, trades and lends. PAWN LOAN: the ticket is "valid for one year", during which you may return to repay the loan plus any fees, or renew. The site states plainly what happens otherwise: "If you're unable to repay the loan or don't return within the year, the item will become the legal property of Queenglad Pawnbrokers and be sold at a reasonable rate." It advertises "zero lending limits on instant cash loans" and claims "some of the lowest interest rates in the GTA" but publishes NO rate — none is stated here because none is published. OUTRIGHT SALE is offered on the same categories. No ID requirement is stated on their site.
orgs.singleAddress: 1200 Queen St W, Toronto, ON M6J 1J6
orgs.locationsNote: Single downtown-west location, operating since 1996. Mon-Sat 10:00am-5:00pm, closed Sunday.
orgs.caution: "Some of the lowest interest rates in the GTA" is a marketing claim with no number published behind it. Get the rate, the fees and the total cost to redeem written on the ticket before handing anything over. Forfeiture of an unredeemed item after one year is stated on their own site.

orgs.name: Williams Pawnbrokers
buys: Jewellery — gold, silver, platinum and precious stones
orgs.dealNote: LOANS ONLY on the strength of their own site. They state "We offer low-interest loans on everything from jewellery to estate items" and offer seasonal storage of pledged items such as golf clubs. Nowhere on the site do they say they will buy an item outright — if you want a sale rather than a loan, phone first. No interest rate, no redemption period and no ID requirement is published. The site states "We do not offer payday loans." Licensed pawnbroker on Church Street since 1950.
orgs.locationsNote: One downtown location on Church Street. Mon-Sat 9:00am-5:30pm, closed Sunday.
orgs.caution: This is a lender, not a buyer, as far as their own site goes — arriving expecting to sell is likely to be a wasted trip. "Low-interest" is their own uncosted word; no rate and no redemption period appear anywhere on the site, so get both in writing on the ticket. An unredeemed pledge is forfeited.

metros.name: Montréal
metros.regulationNote: We could not verify this city’s municipal rules for second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers from an official source, so we state none. Check with the City or the province before relying on anything you read about them elsewhere.

orgs.name: Aux 33 Tours
orgs.dealNote: Buyers are in the shop seven days a week from 11:00 to 17:00 and evaluate what you bring in person. Their page is explicit that no offer or estimate can be provided by phone or by email — the records have to be in front of them. For collections of more than 250 items they will travel to you and evaluate on site.
orgs.singleAddress: 1373 avenue du Mont-Royal Est, Montréal, QC
orgs.locationsNote: One shop on the Plateau. Shop hours: Mon–Wed 10:00–18:00, Thu–Fri 10:00–20:00, Sat–Sun 10:00–18:00. Buyers are available 11:00–17:00 daily. For collections over 250 items the site gives a separate contact, Pierre, at 514-910-3911.
orgs.caution: No payout percentage is published, and the page does not say whether payment is cash or store credit — ask before they start sorting. Since no estimate is possible by phone, you have to carry everything in before you learn what it is worth.

orgs.name: Kenny U-Pull
refuses: Vehicles with an active lien, until the lien is resolved
orgs.dealNote: Outright purchase. You request a quote and, if you accept, they schedule a pickup. Their own page states they offer free towing and pay cash for vehicles in any condition, that they bring the cash to you at pickup, and that they take care of the necessary paperwork.
orgs.locationsNote: Serves Montreal and surrounding areas; the sale is arranged by phone or online quote and the vehicle is collected, rather than handled at a counter.
orgs.caution: No dollar figure is published — the amount depends on the vehicle and is quoted case by case. On liens their page is explicit: if there is an active lien you usually need to resolve it before a licensed scrap yard can legally buy the vehicle, and an undisclosed lien can delay or cancel the transaction.

orgs.name: Maison Edouard
orgs.dealNote: A buying dealer rather than a shop you visit. Their own page states they travel to your home throughout the Greater Montreal region, look at what you have and make an offer. Useful when you are emptying a house and cannot transport things. The site does not state whether the visit is free, nor how payment is made.
orgs.locationsNote: No shop address is published — a mobile buyer covering Greater Montreal. Hours on the site: Mon–Sat 08:00–19:00, closed Sunday.
orgs.caution: No storefront address, no published prices, and the site does not say whether the visit costs anything or how you are paid — establish all three on the phone. Get an itemised offer, and do not let anything leave before a price is agreed for each piece.

orgs.name: Maison du Comte Antiquités
orgs.dealNote: Buys antiques and estate contents outright. Their own site advertises déplacement gratuit — they travel to your home free of charge — and paiement comptant, an immediate cash payment on an agreed transaction. Aimed at estates and successions, so they will look at a whole house rather than a single item.
orgs.locationsNote: No shop address is published — a mobile buyer. No opening hours are listed on the page fetched.

orgs.name: Encore Books and Records
refuses: Books with creased spines, underlining or dog-eared pages
orgs.dealNote: Buys outright at the counter. This is the one payout figure in this list that the business itself publishes, in its own words: it generally offers around 20–25% of the price it will sell the book for, and the same rate applies to records. It also states that if you prefer to be paid in store credit it will raise the offer by 25%.
orgs.locationsNote: One shop in NDG.
orgs.caution: The 20–25% figure is the shop's own published policy — it is the only documented payout benchmark here and a useful sanity check against any percentage quoted to you verbally elsewhere. Condition drives the offer: scratches and warping on records can mean rejection or a reduced offer.

orgs.name: J'Adore La Fripe
refuses: Items they judge unsellable, off-season or off-brand
Items not dry-cleaned or freshly laundered
orgs.dealNote: Consignment, not outright purchase: they sell the item on your behalf and you are paid a commission when and if it sells, so the money arrives later and only on a sale. Their page states commission is based on the value of the item, but the actual percentages are not published in readable form on the site, so no split is recorded here. Intake is by appointment. Clothing must be dry-cleaned or freshly laundered and in new condition. Designer handbags must come with the original receipt or a valid certificate of authenticity; failing that, they offer to authenticate the item for you.
orgs.singleAddress: 2652 rue Notre-Dame Ouest, Montréal, QC H3J 1N7
orgs.locationsNote: One shop in Little Burgundy, between Atwater Market and the Lachine Canal. No opening hours are published on the pages fetched.
orgs.caution: Their page states you will be asked for your contact information and a valid government-issued ID to consign. Because the commission tiers are not published, ask for the split for your specific items in writing before leaving them.

orgs.name: M.M. Metal
orgs.dealNote: Buys metal by weight. Their own page states the service is aimed at commercial sectors such as construction and renovation but is also accessible to the general public, and that a minimum of one kilogram is required for purchase.
orgs.locationsNote: Off-island in Saint-Eustache, north-west of Montreal — worth the drive only for a reasonable load. Hours on the site: Mon–Fri 07:00–16:30, Sat 08:00–11:30.

orgs.name: RUSE Boutique
orgs.dealNote: Consignment. Their own page describes high-end, designer and unique contemporary items made affordable by their consignment concept, and offers consigning as an option if you do not wish to keep an item. The site does not mention buying anything outright. No split, consignment period or payout method is published.
orgs.locationsNote: Montreal. Hours on the site: Mon–Fri 11:00–19:00, Sat–Sun 11:00–18:00. No street address appears on the pages fetched — confirm by phone before travelling.

orgs.name: Recyclage Miller
orgs.dealNote: A scrap yard: you bring the metal in and they pay for eligible material. Their own page states they will pay cash for your batteries, wires, radiators and much more, and that they give price quotes corresponding to current metal market prices. No fixed price can be quoted in advance because scrap is priced against moving commodity markets.
orgs.locationsNote: Single Montréal-Nord yard. No opening hours are published on the page fetched.

orgs.name: Second'Or
orgs.dealNote: Confirmed on the shop's own pawn-shop page: it offers two different transactions. One is an outright sale — you hand over the item for cash and it is gone. The other is a prêt sur gage, a pawn loan, which is secured credit: the shop lends you money against the item, and you get the item back only if you repay. An unredeemed item is forfeited to the shop. The site publishes no loan term, fee or interest figure of any kind.
orgs.singleAddress: 954 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, Montréal, QC H2L 1Z1
orgs.locationsNote: One downtown/Village location. Hours on the site: Mon–Fri 09:30–18:00, Sat 10:00–17:00, closed Sunday.
orgs.caution: The site states you must bring valid photo ID. Pawning and selling are two different contracts with different consequences — establish which one you are being offered before you hand the item over, and ask for the loan cost in writing if it is a pawn loan.

metros.name: Vancouver
metros.localNote: PAWN LOAN VERSUS SALE — THESE ARE TWO DIFFERENT TRANSACTIONS. The money can look similar on the day. A sale is final: the item is gone and you keep the cash. A pawn is secured credit: you receive less than the item is worth, you owe the principal plus interest, and if you do not redeem it in time the item is forfeited and the shop sells it. You do not receive any balance of the item's value. Of the shops below, Roath's is the only one publishing a rate: 7.5% per month flat, stated as a 90% APR, on loans of $10 to $100,000 over a term running to 90 days. Every other pawnbroker here advertises competitive rates without publishing a number. WHAT OUTLETS TYPICALLY PAY. Only three businesses here publish a payout percentage against resale value: Turnabout (25-60% outright, 40-80% consignment), Mine & Yours (30-50% cash, 40-60% store credit, 50-80% consignment) and Audiopile (one third to one half of a record's value in cash). Antique Warehouse publishes a consignment split of 40% to the consignor for the first 60 days and 30% after. Every other business leaves it unstated, and no percentage has been inferred or estimated for them — where a field is empty, the business does not publish the number, so ask them directly. VEHICLES. I could not verify any fixed-premises auto salvage yard in Metro Vancouver that publishes its buying terms, and no "cash for cars, free towing" operator has been included: they advertise headline figures while publishing no yard address or licence, which is the profile to avoid. ABC Recycling does list end-of-life vehicles among its accepted materials at its licensed yards. Separately, SCRAP-IT (scrapit.ca, a member of the EcoForward Solutions family of programs, 604-868-6935, info@scrapit.ca) offers a $300 cash incentive for retiring a qualifying older vehicle, paid by electronic funds transfer once the scrap yard confirms the vehicle was scrapped, with approval stated within 2 business days. That is a rebate program, not a buyer, and is worth checking before accepting a private offer. This page describes how these transactions work. It does not tell you which to choose, and nothing here is financial advice.
metros.regulationNote: MUNICIPAL RULES ARE WHAT ACTUALLY AFFECT YOU. I could not verify the claim that British Columbia has no pawnbroker statute in force, so that claim has been removed rather than published. What is confirmed is Vancouver's Secondhand Dealers and Pawnbrokers By-law No. 2807, consolidated for convenience to 16 September 2025 (amended to include By-law No. 14443), read directly from the City's own consolidated text at https://bylaws.vancouver.ca/2807c.pdf. BRING PHOTO ID OR YOU WILL BE TURNED AWAY. Both secondhand dealers (buying outright) and pawnbrokers (lending) must confirm your identity by "picture identification" and record a complete description of it and the name of the authority that issued it (ss. 2.2(b), 3.2(b)). The by-law defines picture identification (s. 1.2) as one of the following, bearing a photograph of the holder: a valid driver's licence issued by a Canadian province or territory; a BC Services Card or other photo identity card issued by the Province of British Columbia; a passport issued by a legitimate government; a certificate of Indian status; a certificate of Canadian citizenship; a conditional release card issued by Correctional Services Canada; or a valid Canadian permanent resident card. A credit card, a bus pass or an expired licence does not qualify. The dealer must also record your name, residence or street address and birth date; a complete description of the property including make, model and serial number; the price paid or the amount advanced; the precise date and hour; and any identifying marks (ss. 2.2, 3.2). Other confirmed by-law facts: - You must be at least 18. A dealer must not purchase from, and a pawnbroker must not take a pawn from, anyone under 18 (ss. 2.15, 3.15). - No evening deals. A dealer must not purchase property, and a pawnbroker must not take property in pawn, between 6 p.m. of one calendar day and 6 a.m. of the next (ss. 2.13, 3.13). A shop may be open, but it cannot take your item in. - Anything whose serial number or other identifying marking has been wholly or partially tampered with or removed will be refused outright (ss. 2.14, 3.14). - Police reporting is daily. Shops on electronic registers transmit entries to the Chief Constable electronically (ss. 2.11, 3.11); shops on handwritten registers must hand-deliver a photocopy to the Chief Constable at the Vancouver Police Department, 3585 Graveley Street, between 8:30 a.m. and 10:30 a.m. on each business day (ss. 2.10, 3.10). Registers are kept within BC for seven years after the last entry (ss. 2.9(b), 3.9(b)). Selling second-hand goods in Vancouver is a recorded transaction, not an anonymous one. - Holding period. A shop cannot repair, alter, dispose of or remove an item for the longer of 35 business days (electronic register), 49 business days (handwritten register), or the number of business days the police direct, not exceeding 90 days (ss. 2.19, 3.20). If you pawned rather than sold, s. 3.19 preserves your right to reclaim the item inside that window by paying the debt and interest owing. - A shop licensed as both must physically separate purchased goods from pawned goods and individually tag each item to show the date and whether it was purchased or taken in pawn (s. 2.21) — a useful sign of a properly licensed operator. - In the Downtown Eastside, both secondhand dealers and pawnbrokers may only remain open from 6:00 a.m. to 2:00 a.m. (ss. 2.23, 3.21). Burnaby, Surrey and Richmond license under their own bylaws, so holding periods and reporting hours differ there; I did not read those bylaws, so call ahead if your shop is outside the City of Vancouver. SCRAP YARDS ASK FOR ID TOO. Richmond Steel Recycling states all material suppliers must provide valid government-issued photo ID to sell scrap metal. ABC Recycling requires a valid driver's licence or other government-issued ID and that you drive in with a four-wheel vehicle — bicycles, motorcycles and taxis are not allowed.

metros.name: Calgary
metros.localNote: NO PAYOUT PERCENTAGE APPEARS ANYWHERE IN THIS LIST EXCEPT WHERE A BUSINESS PUBLISHED IT ITSELF. Two businesses publish their own splits: Wilder's Consignment House (40% on accessories and apparel, 50% on handbags and small leather goods under $1,000, 60–70% over $1,000) and Fair's Fair Books (trade credit covers 80% of a book's price with the remaining 20% paid by cash or card; a book with a Fair's Fair sticker earns 50% of its value in store credit). Every other business in this list — every pawn shop, every gold buyer, every scrap yard, every electronics buy-back — publishes no rate, no percentage and no interest figure. That absence is itself the most useful fact on this page, and no figure should ever be invented to fill it. The honest line for a reader is that an offer reflects what the shop must sink into storage, testing and shelf time before it resells the item, and that two or three quotes is the only reliable way to find the range for your particular item. THE FOUR TRANSACTIONS, SORTED BY WHEN THE MONEY ARRIVES. This is the single most useful way to organise the page for someone clearing a house. 1. CASH TODAY, ITEM GONE FOR GOOD. Pawn shops buying outright, PayMore Chinook for devices, Canada Gold for precious metals, Play It Again Sports for gear (paid by cheque), CD Trader and Fair's Fair Inglewood for media, the scrap yards by weight, Alberta Cash for Cars for vehicles. 2. A LOAN YOU MUST REPAY TO GET YOUR ITEM BACK. All four pawn shops offer this alongside buying. It is secured credit, not a sale. If you do not repay within the term, the item is forfeited. None of them publishes a rate. 3. MONEY IN WEEKS OR MONTHS, AND ONLY IF IT SELLS. Wilder's Consignment House (90 or 180 days depending on price, marked down after 45), Reclaim Vintage (consignment offered, no rate published), Play It Again Sports. 4. FREE REMOVAL WITH PAYMENT ON COLLECTION. Mr. Mansfield Vintage for mid-century furniture (free pickup Alberta-wide, paid on collection), Bare Wire Recycling for scrap (pickup requests through their site), Alberta Cash for Cars for vehicles (free towing, paid before loading), and Wilder's for 15+ consignment items. Readers who cannot lift or transport things need this group surfaced first. NARROWNESS IS THE RULE, NOT THE EXCEPTION. Almost every business here wants a thin slice of what is in a house. Mr. Mansfield and Reclaim want mid-century teak and walnut and little else. Wilder's wants luxury labels in sizes 4–14, in perfect condition, current within three years. Chinook's Fair's Fair will only take back books it sold. Play It Again buys seasonally. Set the expectation that most of a household goes to the donation and disposal routes, not the resale ones.

metros.name: Edmonton
metros.localNote: Pawning and selling are two different transactions, and confusing them is where people lose things. A pawn is a loan secured on your item: you keep a claim on it only for the agreed term, and if you do not return and repay in full the item is forfeited and goes on the shop's sales floor. Selling outright ends your claim the moment you take the money. All three Edmonton pawn shops here - Pioneer Jewellery & Loan, West End Exchange and Uncle Ed's Exchange - state on their own sites that they do both, so you must ask which one you are being offered. Only one of them publishes a loan term at all: West End Exchange states "You have 30 days (plus 7 days grace) to return for your items." None of the three publishes an interest rate, a service or storage charge, or a total cost to repay. If you are pawning rather than selling, ask for the loan agreement in writing and read the redemption date and the total repayment figure before you hand anything over. Which of the two suits you is your decision, not ours. Take photo ID. Two of the businesses here publish hard ID rules of their own: Uncle Ed's Exchange states "ALL CUSTOMERS MUST PRODUCE 2 (TWO) PIECES OF IDENTIFICATION, ONE PIECE MUST BE VALID PHOTO ID" and "YOU MUST BE 18 YEARS OF AGE. THIS IS THE LAW." Edmonton Gold requires being "18 years of age or older" and "A valid government-issued photo ID," which it says is required by law. PayMore requires "valid government-issued identification." Turning up with a box of goods and no ID is a wasted trip, and this catches out people clearing a parent's house while carrying someone else's possessions. No payout percentages appear anywhere on this page, and that is deliberate. Not one of these fourteen businesses publishes what it pays relative to resale value, and no credible figure was found for any category. Treat any "pawn shops pay X% of value" number you see elsewhere as unsourced. The one concrete pricing statement any of them makes is General Recycling's: "The price of metal differs depending on the type of metal and can fluctuate from day to day."
metros.regulationNote: We could not verify this city’s municipal rules for second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers from an official source, so we state none. Check with the City or the province before relying on anything you read about them elsewhere.

orgs.name: Architectural Clearinghouse

orgs.dealNote: They buy selectively and want photographs first: "We do buy. But it's not a garage sale. Send photos and we'll tell you straight whether we want it," and "If you're not sure, send photos before you load anything. We'd far rather tell you honestly over email than have you make the trip for nothing." They are upfront that "Sometimes we buy them, sometimes we just take them out" - removal is not the same as payment. They will also walk a site before demolition and pull out what is worth keeping, and note "It works best when we're brought in early."
orgs.caution: Payment terms are not published, and free removal is not a purchase. Establish clearly whether a given job is a purchase or a no-cost removal before any work starts. They state they can only take material in resaleable condition.

Jewellery, gold, diamonds, watches, precious stones, pearls
Mirrors, rugs, bookcases, silverware, wardrobes, armoires, vanities

If your jewellery has meaningful gemstones, have it assessed as jewellery before selling it to a metal buyer.

For fast sellers they say "If your item is a high demand/popular seller we may offer a direct buy out" - that is an outright sale, paid immediately rather than after a buyer is found. On consigned items: "Once the consigned item has sold, the consignor is paid via email money transfer or cheque."

orgs.dealNote: You bring metal to the yard, it is weighed, and you are paid by weight at the grade and the day's rate. A bin service is available separately if you have the volume to justify a container.

orgs.name: Arley's Pawn Shop

Under the Pawnbrokers Act the pawnticket must state the rate of interest charged and the sum lent, so the rate is on the ticket even when it is not on the website. They publish per-gram buying prices for 9k through 24k gold and for sterling silver; those move with the metal market, so check the figure on the day. Their site also advertises a 0% interest layaway plan, which is a separate thing again.

They publish live per-karat buying rates on their site with a last-updated date; those move with the metal market, so read the figure on the day you go rather than relying on one quoted anywhere else.
orgs.locationsNote: One storefront. Hours per their site: closed Monday, Tue-Sun 11am-6pm. Free parking behind the building.
orgs.caution: Scrap gold is paid on metal weight and purity, not on what the piece cost or on any antique or design value. Testing here is described as free and non-binding, so a second opinion elsewhere costs only time.

orgs.name: Howard's Pawn Shop
orgs.dealNote: Their site describes "Buying, Selling, and Trading of New and Used" goods, and separately offers "30-day CA$H loans on your items", which is a loan secured on the item rather than a sale. They also do gold repair and sizing. Payment methods listed on their site: "Cash, Debit, Credit, E-Transfer, Apple Pay, PayPal". No interest rate, fee schedule or loan-to-value figure is published.
orgs.singleAddress: 1052 St. Laurent Blvd, Unit 1, Ottawa, ON K1K 3B4
orgs.locationsNote: Single St. Laurent Boulevard storefront.
orgs.caution: The same premises also advertises payday loans, a separate credit product with its own requirements (their site lists 90 days of banking history, recent pay stubs and a pre-authorized debit authorization). Selling an item outright, taking a 30-day loan against it, and taking a payday loan are three distinct transactions. Nothing about walking in to sell goods obliges you to discuss credit.

orgs.name: Palmer Recycling
orgs.dealNote: A weigh-in scrap yard in south Ottawa that buys "all scrap metal". Their site does not state the payment method or the price basis, so ask when you call. For several tonnes or more they supply a roll-off container, and they will collect heavy equipment over about 4 tonnes that cannot be brought in.
orgs.singleAddress: 3191 Albion Rd. South, Ottawa, ON K1V 8Y3
orgs.locationsNote: One yard. Hours per their site: Mon-Thu 8am-5pm, Fri 8am-4pm, Sat 8am-12pm, closed Sunday. Second line 613-521-5972.
orgs.caution: Their site states the scale closes 15 minutes before closing, so arriving at the posted closing time is too late. No prices are published; confirm the rate for your metal by phone before making the trip.

orgs.name: Patrick McGahern Books
buys: individual items and collections of all sizes
orgs.dealNote: An antiquarian dealer whose site states: "We buy individual items and collections of all sizes. We buy rare books in most subjects," with particular interest in the Arctic, Canadiana, voyages and travel, and military history. This is the outlet for one good old book rather than twelve boxes of paperbacks. Their site says they welcome all enquiries; contact them with details before hauling anything in. No payout basis or percentage is published.
orgs.locationsNote: One shop in the ByWard Market area. Hours are not published on their site; phone ahead.
orgs.caution: Their site states they do not buy damaged books, encyclopedias or textbooks. General used paperbacks and book-club editions are not what a rare book dealer is looking for.

orgs.name: PayMore Kanata
orgs.dealNote: A storefront electronics buy-back. Staff evaluate the device and their site states they pay "cash on the spot". Condition is not a bar to an offer: their site says "Working, broken, cracked, water-damaged - bring it in anyway," though condition will affect the number. They ask you to bring "a valid government-issued photo ID", and state they erase personal information from devices in store, in front of you. No payout percentage is published.
orgs.singleAddress: 420 Hazeldean Rd Unit 7, Kanata, ON K2L 4B2
orgs.locationsNote: Kanata is the only Ottawa-area store with a published address, phone and hours (11am-7pm) on their Ottawa page. Other Ottawa-area names appear on the site without addresses, so check before travelling.
orgs.caution: Bring photo ID, chargers and accessories, and know your device passcode and account logins. A device still locked to an account is usually worth little to a buy-back. Back up anything you want to keep before handing it over, because wiping is part of the process.

orgs.name: Spaceman Music
orgs.dealNote: A Gladstone Avenue instrument shop whose site states: "We take trades, buy outright and consign." That means you can ask for all three numbers on the same instrument: a cash offer now, a trade value against something in the shop, or a price they would list it at on consignment. No consignment percentage is published. They also have an on-site service department, which matters because a setup or repair can change what a playable instrument is worth.
orgs.locationsNote: One shop in Centretown. Hours per their site: Mon-Fri 11am-6pm, Sat-Sun 11am-5pm.
orgs.caution: An outright cash offer, a trade credit and a consignment listing price are three different numbers for the same instrument, and only the first is money in hand today. Ask which one you are being quoted.

orgs.name: The Recollective
buys: luxury handbags and clothing (Louis Vuitton, Chanel, Hermes, Gucci, Prada, Dior, Fendi, Givenchy, Burberry, Balenciaga, Saint Laurent, Acne Studios, Isabel Marant)

contemporary brands (Aritzia, Zara, H&M, COS, & Other Stories, Arket, Free People, Mango, Madewell, Sezane, Ralph Lauren, Levi's, Everlane, Smythe, All Saints, Anine Bing, Zadig & Voltaire, Gap, Banana Republic)
refuses: items with wear, holes, pilling or stains
orgs.dealNote: One of the few Ottawa consignors that publishes its split. Their consign page states: "For items SOLD for less than $200, you earn 30% cash or 40% store credit. Sold for $200-$500, you earn 50%. Sold for $500-$700, you earn 60%. Sold for $700+, you earn 70%." Separately they offer a "bag buyout" on contemporary pieces at roughly 20% of resale price, paid in cash at drop-off, which is an outright sale rather than consignment. Items must arrive washed and folded in a bag, with your name and email labelled inside and outside.
orgs.locationsNote: One shop in Westboro. Hours per their site: Wed 12-4, Thu-Fri 12-5, Sat-Sun 12-4. Contact is by email: hello@shoptherecollective.com, or management@shoptherecollective.com. No phone number is published on their site.
orgs.caution: Their site states it may take up to 60 days after drop-off to receive pricing, and that unsold items are automatically donated to their charity partner 60 days after pricing. If you want unsold items back, those are the dates to diarise.

orgs.name: Total Home Consignment
refuses: items that are not clean or missing working parts
orgs.dealNote: A furniture and decor consignment showroom that does publish its terms. Their site states items are placed in the showroom for a 90-day term; the consignor receives 50% of the selling price for the first 60 days and 40% for the last 30 days. The price is reduced every 15 days to increase the chance of a sale. Email photos to info@totalhomeconsignment.com for a free evaluation; items need pre-approval and must be clean with all working parts. Delivery to the store is the consignor's responsibility, though they can recommend a delivery service.
orgs.singleAddress: 1860 Bank Street Unit 4, Ottawa, ON K1V 7Z8
orgs.locationsNote: One showroom on Bank Street, described on their site as behind the Beer Store. Hours: closed Monday, Tue-Sat 10am-5pm, Sun 12pm-5pm.
orgs.caution: Consignment is not a sale. You are paid only if and when the item sells, at whatever price it has been marked down to by then. Their site states that at the end of the term unsold items must be picked up or mutual arrangements made, and that items left unclaimed are "considered abandoned and are donated or sold for storage fees."

orgs.name: Valamode
orgs.dealNote: An Ottawa luxury resale business offering, per its own site, consignment, buyouts (outright purchase), a "closet cleanse" service and estate management. No commission, split or payout percentage is published on the site. The showroom is "BY APPOINTMENT ONLY" and contact is by email to info@valamode.com to book.
orgs.locationsNote: Their site describes an Ottawa showroom by appointment only. No street address and no phone number are published on the site; contact is by email to arrange an appointment.
orgs.caution: A buyout and a consignment are different transactions and produce different numbers for the same item. No address is published on their site, so confirm where you are going before travelling with valuables.

metros.name: Winnipeg
metros.localNote: Bring government-issued photo ID. Two of the precious-metals buyers below publish an ID requirement on their own sites, and it is a safe assumption anywhere you are selling goods for cash. Record serial numbers before anything leaves the house. It costs nothing and it is the one thing that lets an item be identified later, whether it was stolen from you or you are the seller being asked about it. Beware of operators that rank for "Winnipeg" searches but are not here. Check that the phone number is a 204 number and that a physical Winnipeg address is published before you load a vehicle. Every business listed below was confirmed against its own website, with a Manitoba address and a Manitoba phone number. Sunday and evening options are thin. Most yards and dealers here are weekday-only, and several close for lunch or stop taking material well before the posted closing time. Buck's Auto Parts is open seven days; the scrap yards are not.
metros.regulationNote: CONFIRMED: Manitoba has no province-wide pawnbroker or secondhand-dealer statute. The index of C.C.S.M. Acts contains no Act titled "Pawnbrokers", "Second-hand", "Secondhand" or "Salvage Dealers". The only provincial mention of a pawnbroker is a definition inside The Personal Property Security Act, C.C.S.M. c. P35, which defines "pawnbroker" as "a person who engages in the business of granting credit to individuals for personal, family or household purposes and who (a) takes and perfects security interests in consumer goods by taking possession of them, or (b) purchases consumer goods under agreements or undertakings, express or implied, that the goods may be repurchased by the seller". ONE PROVISION MATTERS TO ANYONE PAWNING AN ITEM. Section 55(1) of that Act states that Part 6 - "Rights and Remedies on Default" - "does not apply to ... (b) a transaction between a pledgor and a pawnbroker." Part 6 is the part of the Act that gives an ordinary borrower protections when a secured creditor seizes and sells collateral. Those protections do not apply to a pawn transaction. A full text search of the Act returns the word "pawnbroker" only three times: the English definition, the French definition, and this exclusion. The Act sets no licensing, seller-ID, record-keeping, police-reporting, holding-period or redemption requirements for pawnbrokers. NOT CONFIRMED, AND THEREFORE NOT STATED AS FACT: Winnipeg regulates used-goods and precious-metals dealers municipally, but I could not retrieve the text of the City's business licensing by-law or its licensing pages - every City URL I tried returned 404 or was blocked. So this guide does not assert how many activities the City licenses, the definitions or exclusions for "Used Goods Dealer", "Precious Metals Dealer" or "Used Material Yard", whether a Certificate of Record Review Board from the Winnipeg Police Service is required, any holding period before resale, or any police-reporting duty. I also could not verify the Winnipeg Police Service "Operation Identification" program or its phone number. Anyone who needs those specifics should confirm them with City of Winnipeg Licensing and Bylaw Enforcement via 311 before relying on them. SELLER ID, CONFIRMED FROM THE BUYERS THEMSELVES RATHER THAN FROM ANY REGULATOR: Canada Gold's Winnipeg page states you must be "18 years of age or older" and provide "A valid government-issued photo ID". Winnipeg Gold Buyer's site states "we require a piece of photo ID (to help the authorities ensure the items are not stolen)". Both are the businesses' own published policies. Take government-issued photo ID to any of these outlets.

orgs.name: Bison Books
orgs.dealNote: An antiquarian dealer downtown. Their site states: 'We are always purchasing good books. We seek out, and pay a premium for, valuable books, including rare books, fine bindings, illustrated books, first editions, signed books, and more.' Note where the emphasis falls - the premium is for the scarce end, not for general secondhand stock. Their listed categories include first editions, fine bindings, Indigenous studies, literature, art, children's books and classics. Usefully for a house clearance, the site offers house calls and appraisals alongside book searches, acquisitions consultations and mail orders, and takes appointments through the website - which is the sensible route for anything more than an armful. Payment terms are not published.
orgs.locationsNote: One shop on Graham Avenue, downtown. Store hours are on their Location & Store Hours page rather than the homepage; house calls and appointments are offered.
orgs.caution: They state they pay a premium for valuable books, which is not the same as paying for all books - expect a dealer to take the few items they want and decline the rest, so have a plan for the remainder before you arrive rather than after. If a collection is large or you cannot transport it, ask about the house call rather than boxing everything up first. Do not clean, tape or otherwise tidy an old book before showing it; if in doubt, show it as it is and let the dealer advise.

orgs.name: La Shop Lesage
buys: Household items assessed individually from photographs - they do not publish a category list
orgs.dealNote: Outright purchase, not consignment, and the process is the useful one for a house clearance. Their stated method: send photographs to lashoplesage@gmail.com or telephone, and in their words, 'If we are interested we will purchase your items and pick them up.' So the valuation happens from photographs before anyone moves furniture, and collection is part of the deal when they want the items. No consignment arrangement is mentioned anywhere on the site. They do not publish a list of what they will and will not consider, so send photographs of anything you are unsure about rather than assuming.
orgs.locationsNote: Single shop on Marion Street in St Boniface. Monday to Friday 10am-5pm, Saturday 10am-3pm, closed Sunday, with appointments available outside those hours - the site recommends calling ahead.
orgs.caution: Send clear photographs that include any damage. An offer made on flattering photographs is liable to be revised at the door, and you will have less room to argue once a van is outside. Agree the price for the whole lot before collection is arranged, and establish whether the figure quoted is net of the pickup or whether collection is charged separately - the site does not say.

orgs.name: Recycle Your Ride
orgs.dealNote: You describe the vehicle and they quote. The site asks for 'year, make, model, condition and pickup location', adding that 'Keys, ownership information and photos can also help', through an online form they say takes about three minutes. Their stated terms on collection: 'Pickup is free when Recycle Your Ride purchases your vehicle'. No price range is published, and their position is that every vehicle is different - which is the honest answer, and means the only real number is the one you are quoted for your car.
orgs.locationsNote: Based in Lorette, southeast of the city, serving Winnipeg and surrounding Manitoba communities including Headingley, Selkirk, Niverville, Beausejour, Ste. Anne, Morris, Dugald, Anola, Lockport and St. Malo.

orgs.name: Broadway Pawn & Sales
orgs.dealNote: The site states plainly: 'We Buy | We Pawn | We Sell', and separately 'We buy and sell gold!!!'. Buying outright is a straight sale - money for the item, item gone. Pawning is a loan against the item, which you must repay to get it back. The categories explicitly named as bought are gold, silver, diamonds and watches. The site also describes itself as 'a music store, a jewelery store, a furniture store, a tool store, a game and movie store and more', so it is worth asking about instruments, tools, furniture and games - but that line describes what they stock, not a published buying list. No loan terms, rates or redemption period are published. Appraisal is in-store only: the site states 'all customers must come to our shop to get the appraisal'. They also state 'We have cheque cashing!!!', which is a separate financial service.
orgs.locationsNote: One shop, on Broadway just west of downtown.
orgs.caution: Be clear which transaction you are entering. A pawn loan is secured borrowing and the item is forfeited if it is not redeemed; a sale is final. Manitoba's Personal Property Security Act excludes pledgor-and-pawnbroker transactions from the Part 6 default protections that apply to other secured credit. Neither the interest rate nor the redemption period is published on the site, so get both in writing before you sign. Because appraisal is in-store only, budget for the trip, and take photo ID.

orgs.name: Buck's Auto Parts
orgs.dealNote: An established Winnipeg auto recycler running three yards on Springfield Road, each handling different vehicle categories. Their site states: 'If you have a car that is no longer running or just taking up space, we will give you a fair quote and handle the hard part. We buy junk cars and make the process simple, fast, and worth your while.' The route is a quote form, and they say they 'will respond within 24-48 hours'. No price figures are published, and the site does not spell out what paperwork they need or whether towing is included, so establish both by phone. Open seven days, which is unusual for a salvage yard and useful if you can only move a vehicle at the weekend: Monday to Saturday 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM, Sunday and most holidays 10:00 AM - 4:00 PM.
orgs.locationsNote: Three yards at 1550, 1640 and 1650 Springfield Road, each specialising in different vehicle categories.
orgs.caution: Their own navigation labels this 'Donate/Sell Vehicle'. Donating and selling are different outcomes and one of them pays you nothing, so say explicitly which you want and get the answer before the vehicle moves. The quote comes back in 24 to 48 hours rather than on the spot, so do not plan the clear-out around a same-day collection. Confirm whether towing is included and what ownership paperwork they need, and check the registration and insurance cancellation steps with Manitoba Public Insurance.

orgs.name: Canada Gold - Winnipeg
buys: Canadian gold, silver, platinum and palladium bullion
Dental gold and other precious metal items
Scrap gold, silver and platinum in any form
orgs.dealNote: Outright purchase. Their sell-to-us page states that specialists will 'evaluate your items in front of you and provide a free, no-obligation offer based on current market prices', that 'No appointments required', and that 'Almost all payouts are completed the same day'. The evaluation happening in front of you is the useful part - you can ask for the weight and the purity reading as they take them. The site does not state what percentage of spot price they pay, and that figure should not be assumed from anywhere else; ask for the offer expressed as a percentage of spot before you accept, and write down the weight and purity you were quoted. Part of a national chain. Store hours: Monday to Friday 9:30am-6:00pm, Saturday and Sunday 10:00am-5:00pm.
orgs.locationsNote: One Winnipeg store on Corydon Avenue, open seven days. Toll-free line 1-888-219-7001.
orgs.caution: Their site states you must be '18 years of age or older' and provide 'A valid government-issued photo ID' to complete a transaction - do not make the trip without it. Precious metal is bought on weight and purity, so an item whose value lies in its craftsmanship, maker, brand or age is being valued on the wrong axis here; have anything of that kind assessed by a jeweller or collector first, because a scrap sale is irreversible. Getting a second quote costs only time, and the evaluation is free and carries no obligation.

orgs.name: Chochy's Pawn & Swap Shop
buys: Chains, rings, pendants, bracelets, earrings and watches
orgs.dealNote: Two different transactions, and the difference matters. Their site has a 'Buying & Selling' page covering outright purchase and sale, and separately lists 'the pawning process' among their specialties. Selling outright means you hand over the item, take the money, and the item is gone. Pawning is a loan secured on the item: you keep the right to redeem it by repaying the loan plus charges within the agreed period, and if you do not redeem it the item is forfeited to the shop. No loan terms, interest rate, fee schedule or redemption period appears anywhere on the site. Their site also lists 'In-house financing of vehicles' as a specialty, which is a separate credit product again. The site states 'Since 1983 we have been at our same location, and under the same ownership'.
orgs.locationsNote: Single storefront on Selkirk Avenue in the North End.
orgs.caution: Be certain which of the two transactions you are signing, because a pawn loan and a sale have opposite consequences. Manitoba's Personal Property Security Act expressly excludes a pledgor-and-pawnbroker transaction from Part 6, the part of the Act that sets out a borrower's rights and remedies when a secured creditor enforces against collateral. This shop publishes no loan terms, no interest rate, no fees and no redemption period, so ask for all of it in writing at the counter before agreeing to anything, and make sure the paperwork says plainly whether you are selling or pawning.

orgs.name: Gill's New & Used Furniture & Appliances
orgs.dealNote: The only buying statement published on the site is the banner 'We Buy & Sell Furniture - We Deliver'. That is furniture specifically. They also deal extensively in reconditioned appliances - washers, refrigerators, stoves, freezers, dishwashers, dryers - but the site does not state that they buy appliances from the public, only that they sell reconditioned ones, so treat appliances as a question to ask rather than a service to assume. No buying process, prices, or pickup terms for purchases are published at all. They run their own delivery trucks and offer setup and in-house service, but that is for outbound sales.
orgs.locationsNote: One warehouse on Salter Street in the North End. Monday to Friday 9am-6pm, Saturday 9am-5pm, closed Sunday.
orgs.caution: They publish no buying terms whatsoever, so assume nothing about price, collection or what they will take - phone before you move anything. Because they recondition and sell appliances, it is worth asking whether they buy them even though the site does not say so; a working appliance is worth pricing with a dealer like this before it goes to a scrap yard that pays only by weight. Have the model number and age ready and be straightforward about faults.

orgs.name: Industrial Metals
refuses: E-waste is accepted for safe recycling but is not paid for
orgs.dealNote: Drop off at the yard. Their residential page states 'our courteous staff will analyze your materials, weigh them accurately and pay you cash on site'. This is one of the few scrap operations here that publishes a dedicated residential page, so a householder arriving with a single load is an expected customer rather than a nuisance. No per-pound rates are published. The page is explicit that e-waste is handled through their EPRA partnership and that 'While we don't pay cash for these items, we do ensure they are recycled safely' - that is a disposal service, not a sale.
orgs.locationsNote: Messier Street yard in St Boniface. The residential page directs customers to bring material to the yard rather than offering household pickup. Alternate toll-free line 800-567-5116.
orgs.caution: Only the metal is paid for - do not expect money for the electronics you bring along, which they recycle free but do not buy. Clearing a house, it is worth pricing any working appliance with a used-appliance dealer before it goes on the scale, because a scrap yard pays on weight regardless of condition. Weekday hours only, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM Monday to Friday.

orgs.name: Into the Music
orgs.dealNote: A record shop in the Exchange District. The one operational fact they publish about buying, and it is the one that matters: 'We are currently buying vinyl on Mondays, Tuesdays, and Fridays.' Turning up with crates on a Saturday is a wasted trip. Note the word 'currently' - buying days are subject to change, so telephone before loading the car, especially for a large collection. The site does not state whether they pay cash, trade credit or either, does not publish a buying policy for CDs or DVDs, and does not say what they decline, so ask all of it on the phone. Store hours are Monday to Thursday 10:30am-6:00pm, Friday 10:30am-9:00pm, Saturday 10:30am-6:00pm, Sunday 11:00am-5:00pm - but the buying days are the narrower constraint.
orgs.locationsNote: One shop in the Exchange District, at the corner of King and McDermot.
orgs.singleAddress: B-245 McDermot Avenue, Winnipeg, MB R3B 0S6
orgs.caution: Buying days are Monday, Tuesday and Friday and are described as current rather than permanent - call first. Their published buying statement covers vinyl only; do not assume CDs or DVDs will be bought without asking. Ask whether you are being quoted cash or trade credit, because they are different amounts of money and the site does not say which is offered.

orgs.name: Mobile Tech Lab
orgs.dealNote: Straight purchase or trade-in, with a choice of payout. The site states: 'Get same-day cash, e-transfer, or store credit for any phone, tablet, laptop, MacBook, console, or smartwatch', and 'We test broken devices too'. So cash is genuinely on the table, not only repair or store credit. No payout percentage or price guide is published, so the quote is the only number that counts - get it before you hand anything over. They also run a mail-in service for the rest of Manitoba, listing Brandon, Portage la Prairie, Steinbach, Selkirk, Dauphin, Morden and Winkler.
orgs.locationsNote: St Vital storefront on Dakota Street. The company also lists Thompson, MB (300 Mystery Lake Rd, Unit 1160, 204-410-0262) and Prince Albert, SK, plus a Manitoba-wide mail-in option.
orgs.singleAddress: 845 Dakota St, Unit 25, Winnipeg, MB R2M 5M3
orgs.caution: Wipe the device and sign out of every account before you go - factory reset, and on Apple hardware turn off Find My, or the buyer may refuse it or pay less. Remove SIM and memory cards. A store-credit offer and a cash offer are not the same money, so ask which figure you are being quoted.

orgs.name: Orloff Scrap Metals
orgs.dealNote: Paid by weight at the yard. The site states 'Orloff Scrap Metals pays cash for all manner of ferrous and nonferrous scrap metal', from individual, commercial or industrial sources, and invites you to bring material to the yard. No per-pound rates are published anywhere - scrap prices move daily, so phone for the day's rate before loading a trailer. They place bins at commercial and industrial sites with no service fee, but that is a trade service; no residential pickup is offered.
orgs.locationsNote: One yard on King Street in the North End. The lunch closure and the last-entry cutoff are both easy to get caught by.
orgs.caution: Hours are tight and precisely stated: 'Monday - Friday: 8:00 AM - 12:00 PM, 12:30 PM - 4:30 PM', with 'Last entry to the yard is 4:15 PM'. Saturday is 'Selected dates only - call office for details'. They are 'Closed on Holiday Weekends' and 'Closed Between Christmas Day and New Year's Day'. Turning up at 4:20 or on an unannounced Saturday means being turned away. Scrap is paid by weight, not by whether the thing works, so if an appliance still runs it is worth getting a price from a used-appliance dealer before weighing it in. Fridges, freezers and air conditioners contain refrigerant - ask the yard how they want those presented before you load one.

orgs.name: So Over It Luxury Consignment
refuses: Brands outside their published Accepted Luxury Designers and Accepted Contemporary Brands lists
orgs.dealNote: Consignment, not outright purchase - you are paid only after the item sells, and nothing on the site indicates they buy outright. Their consignment page publishes the commission as the consignor's share, in their words 'commission to the consignor'. Contemporary: 'a flat 40% commission to the consignor', or 50% if you take store credit. Luxury: 'All clothing: 30% commission. All items $1,499 and under: 50% commission. All items $1,500+: 60% commission.' Chanel and Hermes: 'All items $1,499 and under: 50% commission. All items $1,500-$2,999: 60% commission. All items $3,000+: 70% commission.' Authentication fees are published separately: 'Standard authentication: $75. Authentication with certificate: $95. Chanel and Hermes authentication: $150.' They publish accepted-designer and accepted-brand lists; check yours against them before booking. No minimum item value and no consignment term are published. Book through the 'Consign Now' flow on the site, or by phone or email.
orgs.locationsNote: Two adjacent units on Academy Road. Unit 101 is So Over It Luxury; unit 100 is So Over It Contemporary.
orgs.singleAddress: 101-394 Academy Rd, Winnipeg, MB (Luxury); 100-394 Academy Rd (Contemporary)
orgs.caution: Consignment means no money until the item sells, and it may not sell. Read the percentages the right way round: the published figure is the consignor's share, not the shop's. Taking store credit rather than cash raises your share on the Contemporary side but locks the proceeds into the shop. Authentication fees are charged separately from the commission, so on a lower-value item a $75 to $150 fee is a large proportion of the return - ask how the fee is applied and whether it is still charged if the item does not sell. No consignment term is published, so ask how long they hold an item and what happens to it at the end.

orgs.name: Winnipeg Gold Buyer
buys: Gold jewellery, damaged or not, valued on weight and purity
orgs.dealNote: Outright purchase with immediate payment. The site states 'Should you choose to sell your items... you will be paid cash on the spot!', describes itself as 'Fully licensed - Competitive market prices', and offers free evaluation. Their what-we-buy page is specific: they buy 'gold jewellery based on its weight and purity, damaged or not', plus 'silver jewellery, silverware (sterling cutlery) and coins' and 'foreign coins, banknotes (paper currency) and war medals'. Broken and damaged jewellery being explicitly welcome makes this a realistic outlet for the odd-earring-and-tangled-chain drawer that turns up in every house clearance. No payout percentage is published.
orgs.locationsNote: Three Winnipeg branches plus Brandon, and the hours differ sharply between them. North Winnipeg: 1147 Henderson Hwy, R2G 1L5, (204) 661-4653, Mon-Fri 10am-6pm, Sat 10am-5pm, closed Sun. South Winnipeg: 628 St Anne's Rd, R2M 4W3, (204) 233-4653, Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri 10am-4pm, closed Wed, Sat 10am-2pm, closed Sun. West Winnipeg: 3127 Portage Ave, R3K 0W4, (204) 832-4653, closed Mon, Tue-Fri 10am-4pm, Sat 10am-2pm, closed Sun. Brandon: 204 Rosser Ave, (204) 728-4653, closed Mon-Tue, Wed-Fri 10am-5pm, Sat 10am-3pm, closed Sun.
orgs.caution: Their site states 'we require a piece of photo ID (to help the authorities ensure the items are not stolen)' - bring it. Check the specific branch before travelling: the South branch closes Wednesdays, the West branch closes Mondays, and both shut at 4pm on the days they do open, so only the Henderson Highway branch keeps anything like full hours. War medals and older coins can carry collector interest that has nothing to do with their metal content, and this is a buyer that values gold by weight and purity - have anything unusual looked at by a collector or numismatist before selling it by weight.

metros.name: Québec City
