metros.name: Kitchener–Waterloo
metros.localNote: PAWN SHOPS — AN HONEST GAP. Kitchener, Cambridge and Guelph do have pawn shops, but this guide deliberately lists none, because not one could be verified to the standard applied here. Several trade only through directory listings or social media with no site of their own. citypawnbrokers.ca does not resolve at all — the DNS lookup fails. cambridgebuyandsell.ca now serves an unrelated online casino, the domain having evidently lapsed and been re-registered. Directory sites confidently list these as operating. Phone any pawn shop and confirm it exists before travelling, and treat third-party listings for this sector as unreliable. PAWNING IS NOT SELLING. These are two different transactions and the difference matters enormously. An outright sale ends your interest in the goods: the money is yours and the item is gone. A pawn is a secured loan. The shop lends you a sum against the item, keeps the item, and you get it back only by repaying the loan plus interest and charges within the redemption period. If you do not redeem it, the item becomes the pawnbroker's absolute property — you keep the cash but lose the goods permanently. Under Ontario law your pawn ticket must state the rate of interest charged (Pawnbrokers Act s. 10); read it before you sign and keep it. Shops that both buy and lend will usually lend less than they would pay to buy outright. Which route suits you is your decision alone — this guide does not advise on it — but be certain which one you are agreeing to. WATCH FOR THE SAME AMBIGUITY OUTSIDE PAWN SHOPS. Guelph Music both buys instruments outright and takes them on consignment; KW Consignment may move unsold goods to auction. In each case the two outcomes are very different for you. Ask which one is on offer. WHAT THE OUTLETS ACTUALLY PAY. This is the number everyone wants and the one most often invented, so read this carefully. After checking every business listed here against its own site, only TWO publish any figure at all, and both are recorded above in their own words: Hello Again states the consignor receives 40% of the selling price, and Janus Books states "We buy for cash or offer 50% more in store credit" — note that the Janus figure is the uplift for taking credit instead of cash, not a share of resale value. Northern Gold Exchange is commonly cited as paying 78% of spot. Their site does not say that. What it says is "Our company started by paying 78% of the current day's spot price" — a statement about how the business began in 2009, not a rate offered today. It has been removed from their record for that reason. The same page's claim that No credible source was found for any general rule about what pawn shops or second-hand buyers typically pay relative to resale value in this region, and none has been invented here. Ask each outlet for its own number, on the day, and get it in writing before you agree. IDENTIFICATION. Only Once Upon A Child states an ID requirement on its own site, and it is emphatic: you cannot sell to them without government photo ID. This is the single most common cause of a wasted trip in this sector. Take photo ID wherever you are selling. TIMING AND STALE LISTINGS. Two of the outlets above — Plato's Closet and Once Upon A Child — publish a Kitchener location page on their brand site that does not render a street address, phone number or hours. Their buying policies are confirmed, but their exact locations are not, so look them up on the brand's store locator before travelling. Habitat for Humanity ReStore in Waterloo and Cambridge, and Recycle Cycles in Kitchener, are excluded here because they accept donations rather than paying for goods — they suit a tax receipt, not cash. PRACTICAL SEQUENCING FOR A HOUSE CLEARANCE. Consignment and auction pay later and only if the item sells; buy-back shops and scrap yards pay on the day. Appointment-only consignors such as Hello Again book weeks ahead — its booking window opens on the last Tuesday of the month and closes once full — so approach them first if you are working to a moving date. Scrap and vehicle buyers price against commodity markets that move daily, so get those quotes on the day you intend to sell rather than weeks in advance. And check the day of the week: Janus Books does not buy on Tuesdays.

metros.name: London
metros.localNote: Thirteen of the fourteen businesses verified against their own websites. The one rejection is the only pawn shop, so as it stands this list contains NO pawn outlet for London — every surviving entry is either an outright sale, a consignment split, or payment by weight. That is an honest outcome and better than publishing unverifiable loan terms, but it means the guide currently has no answer for a reader specifically looking to borrow against an item rather than sell it. If you want pawn covered for London, a shop needs to be sourced and its loan terms read from its own site first. Because the pawn entry is gone, no record on this list describes secured credit. Nothing here is a loan: nothing is pledged, nothing accrues interest, and nothing is forfeited. Worth stating plainly on the page so the distinction is not lost when a pawn shop is added later. Payment-form is the recurring gap. Five businesses that clearly buy from the public — Grooves, Speed City, Odyssey, AIM and to a degree Zubick — do not publish whether they pay cash or trade credit, or at what proportion of resale value. Game Cycle publishes that it pays "cash or store credit" but not how the two compare. No business on this list publishes a payout percentage, so no percentage appears anywhere in the output. That field stays empty rather than estimated. The two genuinely transparent outlets on price are the scrap yards: London Salvage posts dated per-pound rates (verified today, 24 September 2026) and Zubick posts rates updated 23 September 2026. Both carry their own disclaimers that the posted figures are indicative and the yard's price governs. Those figures will go stale within days, so they need either a refetch schedule or a visible "as of" date on the page.

metros.name: Halifax
metros.localNote: Everything below separates what I could verify from what I could not. THE PAWN QUESTION, WHICH MATTERS MORE HERE THAN ANYTHING ELSE. A sale and a pawn are different transactions with different consequences, and the Halifax picture is not what the shop names suggest. Of the three shops in the pawn or precious-metals bracket, only Halifax Buy and Sell states on its own site that it does both — "small collateral loans (pawns) and buying and selling." Most Wanted trades under a pawn name but, checked across its store page, its About page and its home page, advertises outright buying only; pawn appears solely in a sentence about its first store opening in 2009. East Coast Buy and Sell describes buying precious metals and nothing else. So a Halifax reader walking into what looks like a pawn shop is most likely being offered a purchase. A sale is final and the money is yours. A pawn is secured credit: the shop holds the item, you repay to get it back, and if you do not repay by the deadline the item is forfeited and sold. No shop in this list publishes a loan period, fee or rate, so the cost of borrowing cannot be worked out from any website — it has to be quoted in store. Ask which transaction you are being offered, every time. PAYOUT RATES. No business in this list publishes what it pays relative to resale value, and I found no credible source stating a figure for this market, so no such number appears anywhere above. The only percentages here are the two consignment splits, which are the shops' own published tiers: Brilliant Clothing at 45/50/60/70 percent by price band, and Room 152 at 40/50/60/70 percent by price band. Both are the consignor's share of the sale price. Everything else is quoted per item, in person. PHOTO ID. PayMore's own Halifax page tells sellers to bring "a valid government-issued photo ID." That is a verified instruction from one business, not a general rule I could confirm — but taking ID to any buyer of secondhand goods is the cheapest way to avoid a wasted trip. STORE CREDIT, NOT CASH. Agricola Street Books pays in store credit only and buys on scheduled weekends roughly every second month. It is in the list because it genuinely takes books off the public, but anyone clearing a house for money should know before loading the car. Cyclesmith was rejected outright for a stronger version of the same problem. SCRAP. Neither yard publishes rates, and neither can — scrap is priced by daily commodity markets. Phone the morning you go. Fridges, freezers and air conditioners contain refrigerant that normally has to be removed before a yard will take them, which can cost more than the metal is worth. ADDRESSES I COULD NOT CONFIRM. Taz Records does not publish street addresses on the pages I could read, though the Halifax and Dartmouth phone numbers are on its own location pages. Room 152 publishes a phone number on its consignment page but no street address anywhere on the site. Both are in the list because the buying terms are clearly published and the phone numbers are official, but call before driving. GEOGRAPHY. Kenny U-Pull's yard is at Elmsdale, outside HRM, but its own page states an 80 km collection radius covering Halifax and Dartmouth, and it comes to you.
metros.regulationNote: We could not verify this city’s municipal rules for second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers from an official source, so we state none. Check with the City or the province before relying on anything you read about them elsewhere.

When you bring us books during scheduled buyback weekends, you're keeping stories in circulation and getting credit to discover what's next," and "We buy books for store credit every other month." Intake runs on scheduled weekends roughly every second month, not continuously.
orgs.caution: You are paid in store credit, not cash. If you are clearing a house for money rather than for more books, this is the wrong door. Check the shop's calendar for the next buyback weekend before loading the car, because intake is not continuous.

orgs.name: Brilliant Clothing Boutique
orgs.dealNote: Consignment only; no outright purchase is described. The store publishes its split by price band, and these are the consignor's share of the sale price: "$ 0 - 50: 45% | $ 50 - 499: 50% | $ 500 - 999: 60% | $ 1000 & up: 70%." The consignment period is 60 days from acceptance, with a 3-day processing window after drop-off, and unsold items are held 14 days for pickup after that. Payout is not automatic: you email the store on your given date to check your account, and proceeds are either set aside at the store or sent by e-transfer for a $1.50 charge. "We are always accepting Consignment, no appointment necessary, just drop by the store." Items must be "in good condition, and arrive to the store freshly washed."
orgs.caution: You are paid only if the item sells, and only after you contact them — nothing lands in your account automatically. Diarise the 60-day date and the 14-day pickup window.

orgs.name: Dartmouth Metals Ltd.
orgs.dealNote: Their site describes "the purchase, sale, and recycling of metals and e-waste components," and lists private citizens among their clientele alongside industry, business and government, so an individual clearing a house can weigh in. The site does not publish a detailed list of accepted materials, any rates, or the payment method. Phone ahead for the day's price and to confirm they take what you have.
orgs.caution: Scrap prices are set daily by commodity markets, not by any website. Sorting metals before you arrive matters, because a mixed load is generally graded down to the cheapest material in it.

orgs.name: East Coast Buy and Sell Inc.
orgs.dealNote: Outright purchase only. Their own wording: "We purchase gold (all karats), silver jewellery and coins, sterling silver, platinum, diamond jewellery, estate jewellery, scrap gold, gold watches, and more," with "Immediate cash payment — no waiting." Despite the "Buy and Sell" name, the site describes no pawn loan, no collateral lending and no redemption terms. Pricing is said to follow current gold and silver spot rates; no percentage of spot is published, so the figure is unknown until you are quoted in store.
orgs.locationsNote: Two Halifax stores on their own site: 3200 Kempt Rd and 374 Herring Cove Rd, phone 902-480-7296. The same company also lists a store in Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario at 536 Second Line West.
orgs.caution: Precious metal is bought by weight and purity. Ask to see the item tested and weighed, and ask what price per gram is being applied, before agreeing. If you want a loan rather than a sale, note that the site does not describe one.

orgs.name: Esmé & Evee Vintage
refuses: items with major stains, holes or pilling
fast fashion including Shein, Amazon, Garage, H&M, Zara and GAP
orgs.dealNote: They buy outright and pay immediately: "We pay in e-transfer on the spot (or cash if necessary)." There is no fixed formula — "We ask what you're hoping to make, then negotiate from there" — and they are explicit that their price reflects their position as the middleperson between you and the next buyer. Intake is one day a week: "Drop by Wednesdays," and "We recommend 10-15 pieces at a time."
orgs.caution: Wednesdays only for selling, so any other day is a wasted trip for that purpose. Bring items clean and within the quantity they ask for.

orgs.name: Halifax Buy and Sell (Hydrostone)
orgs.dealNote: This is the only shop in this list whose own site confirms it does both. It describes itself as "Specializing in small collateral loans (pawns) and buying and selling new and gently used merchandise." Those are two different transactions. Selling outright ends your claim on the item: the money is yours and the item is theirs. A pawn is a loan secured on the item: you get cash now, the shop holds the item as collateral, and you repay to get it back. If the loan is not redeemed within the agreed period the item is forfeited and sold. The site publishes no loan period, no fee and no rate, so the cost of borrowing is not knowable from the website.
orgs.caution: Confirm at the counter which of the two transactions you are being offered. No loan period, fee or rate is published anywhere on the site, so ask for the full terms in writing before pledging anything.

orgs.name: John Ross & Sons Ltd.
buys: copper (valves, connections, wire, plumbing and tubing)
aluminum (siding, wheels, window frames, wire, furniture, cans)
stainless steel and nickel alloys (sinks, cookware, BBQ grills, tool steel)
orgs.dealNote: A weigh-in yard: you bring the metal to the scale and are paid on weight and grade. Their buying page states "Regardless of the quantity, we'll buy your metal!" so small household loads are in scope, and the published list is not exhaustive — they invite a call if you are unsure. They publish no per-pound rates anywhere on the site. Scrap prices track commodity markets and move week to week, so the only reliable price is the one the yard quotes on the day.
orgs.locationsNote: Halifax head yard: 171 Chain Lake Drive, B3S 1B3, 902-450-5633, Mon-Fri 7am-5pm, Sat 7am-12pm. Goodwood steel yard: 21 Mills Dr, B3T 1P3, 902-479-0344, same hours. Harbour Metals, also on their locations page, is at 29 Pettipas Dr, Dartmouth, B3B 1K1, 902-468-6787, Mon-Fri 8am-5pm, Sat 8am-12pm.
orgs.caution: Phone for the day's price before loading up, since nothing is published. Fridges, freezers and air conditioners contain refrigerant and yards normally require it removed first — ask what they need before you haul one across town.

orgs.name: Most Wanted (Dartmouth)
orgs.dealNote: Trades under a pawn name but the site describes outright purchase only: "We buy gold, silver, coins and jewellery, tested and weighed in front of you" and "We buy tools, phones, instruments and more, cash on the spot." Their About page mentions pawn only in the past tense, describing the first store opening on 12 May 2009 in Charlottetown "as a small but full-featured pawnshop." Checked across the site, no pawn loan, collateral loan, lending or redemption terms are published anywhere. So what is advertised here is a sale: final, and the money is yours.
orgs.singleAddress: 1245 Cole Harbour Road, Dartmouth, NS B2V 1N1
orgs.caution: The name says pawn; the advertised transaction is purchase. Ask which one you are being offered before handing anything over, because a sale cannot be undone and a pawn loan has to be repaid to get the item back.
orgs.nameNote: Trades as a pawn shop, but what it advertises is an outright purchase. Ask which one you are being offered.

orgs.name: PayMore Halifax and Dartmouth
orgs.dealNote: Outright purchase, paid on the spot: "payment is immediate once you accept an offer, so you can often be in and out in a single visit." They say they "buy all kinds of electronics in any condition" and evaluate on the spot, so the offer follows the test rather than being quoted in advance. Pricing is described as based on real local demand and device condition. They publish no percentage of resale value.
orgs.locationsNote: Halifax: 362 Lacewood Drive Unit 15, B3S 1L8, (902) 417-4040. Dartmouth: 644 Portland Street Unit 6, B2W 2M3, (902) 417-3888.
orgs.caution: Their own instructions say to bring "a valid government-issued photo ID." Sign out of accounts and wipe any device before handing it over — your own sign-out is what makes the device resellable.

orgs.name: Room 152 Clothing Boutique
orgs.dealNote: Consignment, paid at the end of each cycle: "Each consignment period is two months, at the end of which the consigner receives" a share of what sold. Their published tiers: "40% of the sale price of items under $150," 50% from $150 to $499, 60% from $500 to $999, and "70% of the sale price of items valued from $1000 & up." They take items from a list of approved brands, which the consignment page sets out. No appointment: drop off Wednesday, Thursday or Friday, 10-5, and "Please keep your drop offs to 20 items or less."
orgs.locationsNote: The consignment page gives a phone number but no street address, and no address appears on the site's home page or footer either. Call before you load the car so you know where you are going.
orgs.caution: Money arrives only at the end of the two-month period, and only for what actually sold. What they accept is seasonal — winter coats are on the refused list — so check that the season fits before dropping off.

orgs.name: Taz Records
refuses: more selective about easy listening, classical, big band and swing
orgs.dealNote: They buy directly from the public: "We purchase records, CDs, blurays, DVDs, and even some books and memorabilia." Genre matters — "We purchase all genres of music but are more selective about easy listening, classical, big band and swing than we are rock, metal, punk, blues, jazz, and hip-hop." Nothing is quoted sight unseen: "We do not do appraisals and we will not commit to a price without first seeing the items." The range they give is wide: "Assuming condition checks out we might pay a couple dollars or a couple hundred depending on the item." The page does not state whether payment is cash or store credit.
orgs.locationsNote: Halifax store phone (902) 422-5976 and Dartmouth counter inside Morley's Coffee (902) 407-3899, both taken from their own location pages. metros.name: Victoria
metros.localNote: PAWN LOAN VERSUS SALE - the distinction that costs people their possessions. A pawn or collateral loan is secured borrowing: the shop lends you cash, keeps your item, and you get the item back only by repaying the loan plus interest within the agreed period. If it is not repaid, the item is not returned. An outright sale is final and there is nothing to redeem. The same shop will often offer both on the same item, at different amounts, across the same counter, and it is on you to know which one you are signing. Two businesses in this guide offer loans as well as purchases - The Bay Street Broker, whose own wording is that they hold your item until you return to pay the interest, and Old 'N' Gold, which offers collateral-based cash loans on jewellery and precious metals alongside outright sale, trade and consignment. NEITHER publishes an interest rate, a loan term, or a redemption deadline, and we will not guess at one. Ask for the written pawn ticket and read those three things before the item leaves your hands. Short-term secured credit is expensive relative to the sum borrowed; whether that trade is worth it is your call, not ours. WHAT WE COULD NOT FIND OUT, STATED PLAINLY. No Victoria business in this guide publishes what it pays as a percentage of resale value, with three exceptions, all in consignment: Recertified Furniture (50% of net sale amount, and upfront purchases 15%-30% lower than the consignment payout range), A La Mode (40% cash, 50% store credit, 50% cash on top luxury labels) and Cook Street Vintage (50% of selling price). The Bay Street Broker takes 25% plus taxes on consignment. MONA and Super Chance do not publish their splits at all - ask before you leave anything. Every other business quotes case by case, and any "pawn shops typically pay X%" figure you read elsewhere should be treated as invented unless the shop itself says it. CONSIGNMENT HAS A DEADLINE AND IT IS NOT IN YOUR FAVOUR. Consignment pays more than an outright sale but pays later and only if the item sells, and every consignment business here disposes of unsold goods: Cook Street Vintage donates items unclaimed 7 days after a 2-month contract expires; MONA donates at the end of the 3-month contract and will not return items under $100 at all; A La Mode donates two weeks after payout and voids all monies after 6 months. If you are working to a moving date, diarise the contract end date the moment you sign. VICTORIA GEOGRAPHY. The 700-1100 block of Fort Street is the centre of gravity for anything small and valuable - Old 'N' Gold at 742, Russell Books at 747, Britannia Coins at 835 and MONA at 1037 are minutes apart on foot, so one afternoon downtown can produce competing quotes on jewellery, coins, books and clothing. Watch the short hours: Old 'N' Gold closes at 4pm and is shut all weekend, Britannia is closed Sunday and Monday. The scrap and vehicle end is the opposite - Williams' yards are out at Munns Rd and Langford, Malahat Auto Wrecking is up the highway, and those are phone-first or they-come-to-you jobs. Take non-ferrous metal to Williams' Munns Rd yard, not Millstream, which their site says takes iron and steel only. ONE GENUINE GAP. We could not verify a single Victoria electronics buyer that pays cash on the spot. The national trade-in chain we checked pays in store credit and we could not confirm it has a Victoria branch at all, so it is not in this guide. In practice the cash market for used electronics in Victoria runs through the pawn shops and private sale.
metros.regulationNote: CONFIRMED AND BINDING: SCRAP METAL. British Columbia's Metal Dealers and Recyclers Act, SBC 2011 c. 22 (https://www.bclaws.gov.bc.ca/civix/document/id/complete/statreg/11022_01) governs the sale of "regulated metal" - defined as an item substantially made of non-ferrous metal, excluding used metal cans or containers for food, beverages or paint, and metal domestic or household products normally recycled to avoid waste. The Act's definition of non-ferrous metal covers aluminum, copper (including brass and bronze), lead, magnesium, nickel and zinc, and expressly "does not include gold, platinum or silver". A person selling regulated metal must present prescribed identification to the dealer at the time of the transaction. The dealer must record a description of the metal (type, weight, distinguishing marks), the date, time and value of the transaction, the employee's name, and the seller's name, address, telephone number, a description of the identification presented, where the metal came from, the details of anyone who delivered it, and any vehicle used - and must then provide that information to the local police authority within the prescribed period. Practical effect: arriving at a Victoria yard with copper pipe or aluminum and no photo ID means being turned away, and you should be able to say where the metal came from. Note the carve-out: selling gold or silver jewellery, coins or bullion to a Fort Street dealer is NOT covered by this Act. NOT CONFIRMED - DO NOT TREAT AS LAW: PAWNBROKERS AND SECONDHAND DEALERS. We were not able to retrieve the text of any City of Victoria pawnbroker or secondhand-dealer bylaw, and we make no claim here about what provincial or municipal law requires of pawnbrokers, holding periods, or police reporting in Victoria. What we can document is what three businesses state on their own sites: The Bay Street Broker says that for pawns every transaction must be done with 2 pieces of ID; Williams Scrap Iron & Metals says that, abiding by BC laws and regulations, it asks customers to have government ID when bringing in material. Assume ID is required everywhere in this guide and that it will be recorded, and confirm any holding period or reporting rule with the shop itself.

orgs.name: Erik's Unwanted Vehicle Removal
orgs.locationsNote: A mobile removal service covering Greater Victoria, operating since 2002, open Monday to Sunday 8am-5pm. Treat it as a they-come-to-you operation rather than a yard you drop into - phone first.
orgs.dealNote: They quote on the vehicle or the metal and pick it up. Their site says that in many cases where there is still value to your scrap metal they may also offer cash for it - note the conditional wording, cash is not guaranteed on every load. The site advertises a range of $70 to $2000 for vehicles or scrap metal; that is an advertising range spanning almost thirty-fold, not a quote, so the only number that matters is the one they give you for your specific vehicle.
orgs.caution: Their site does not state what ownership paperwork or identification is needed to hand over a vehicle. Ask on the phone what they need from the registered owner, and get the cash figure confirmed before the tow truck is booked rather than after the car is on the deck.

orgs.name: Malahat Auto Wrecking / Cash 4 Junkers
orgs.locationsNote: The yard is at Malahat, north of Victoria; their site says they have operated in the Victoria area for more than 40 years. Junk-car removal across Greater Victoria runs through Cash 4 Junkers on (778) 977-1333, Monday to Friday 8am-4:30pm, covering Victoria, Langford, Colwood, Esquimalt, Saanich, Sidney, North Saanich, Mill Bay, Malahat, Cobble Hill, Duncan, Brentwood Bay and Central Saanich.
buys: Junk, scrap and non-running cars and trucks
orgs.dealNote: They quote per vehicle and, in their own words, pay you your cash on the spot during pickup. No price schedule is published anywhere on either site - the offer is per vehicle.
orgs.caution: Neither site states what ownership documents or ID are required, and neither states in plain words that towing is free, so confirm both on the phone. Note also that the Malahat Auto Wrecking site links to Cash 4 Junkers as its own junk-car removal service, so a quote from each is not two independent quotes - ring an unconnected buyer if you want a genuine comparison.

orgs.name: Recertified Furniture
orgs.locationsNote: Showroom in Victoria. The consignment page gives showroom hours of Monday and Tuesday 1-5pm, Wednesday to Saturday 10-5, closed Sunday, and links to a map rather than printing a street address. No phone number is published on the page, only a contact form.
orgs.dealNote: One of only two businesses in this guide that publishes what immediacy costs you. CONSIGNMENT, in their words: on most items, receive 50% of the net sale amount of the item, paid by e-transfer on the 15th or 30th of the month, the first payout period after your item sells. OUTRIGHT PURCHASE, in their words: for upfront purchases they offer 15%-30% lower than the consignment payout range.
orgs.caution: Pickup is not free, it is deferred. Their site states the cost of pickup is applied to your consignment account and not charged to you upfront, which means it comes out of your eventual payout rather than being waived. Delivering the furniture yourself avoids it. Consignment also means you are not paid until the item actually sells.

orgs.name: Russell Books
orgs.locationsNote: Book trade counter in the Fort Street store. Appointments are booked online and the booking calendar is updated Saturday mornings; only open appointments appear on it.
buys: Books of all kinds, from antiquarian and rare to current bestsellers, with condition as the primary concern
refuses: Books in bad condition - loose pages, cracked spines, odours, heavy marking, rips and tears
orgs.dealNote: The detail that matters most: they generally deal in STORE CREDIT, which you can use on anything they sell in store and which never expires. Their site says cash is offered only for large amounts of desirable books or extremely valuable books, at the buyer's discretion. Appraisal takes roughly 10-25 minutes while you wait nearby, and anything they do not take is handed back.
orgs.caution: If you are clearing a house and need money rather than credit, say so at the counter, because credit is the default and cash is the exception. Their site says that with more than 1000 books you may be eligible for a house call.

orgs.name: A La Mode Consignment
orgs.locationsNote: One store in Oak Bay Village, Tuesday to Saturday 10am-4pm. Consignment is by appointment - their site says to book by calling during business hours.
buys: Brands such as Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Prada and YSL
refuses: Mass-market brands such as H&M and Forever 21
orgs.dealNote: The most transparent split in this guide, published on their own site: the consignor receives 40% payout in cash, or 50% in store credit. Top luxury labels - they name Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Prada and YSL - receive 50% cash. Payouts are made on the 1st and 15th of the month in store by cash; an e-transfer instead costs an extra $2 and a mailed cheque an extra $5, so the convenient payment methods are the ones that shrink your payout.
orgs.caution: Their site states that all monies become null and void after 6 months, and that unclaimed merchandise is donated two weeks after payout. If you consign and then forget about it, you can end up with neither the money nor the clothes. Items must arrive laundered and on hangers - items in garbage bags will be declined.

orgs.name: Britannia Coins and Estates
orgs.locationsNote: Fixed shop on Fort Street. Their site gives hours of Tuesday to Saturday 10:30am-4pm, closed Sunday and Monday, and recommends appointments for their undivided attention.
orgs.dealNote: They buy outright, from small collections up to entire estates, and state that appraisals are free. No payout percentage or rate is published anywhere on the site.
orgs.caution: A free appraisal from a buyer is not an independent appraisal - the person valuing the item is the person who wants to buy it. For a collection of any size it is worth getting a second quote elsewhere before accepting.

orgs.name: Cook Street Vintage
orgs.locationsNote: One store. Hours on their site: Wednesday to Saturday 11am-5pm, Sunday noon-5pm, and by appointment.
refuses: Glass, ceramic or pottery items with chips or cracks
orgs.dealNote: Their site states the consignor receives 50% of selling price, on a 2 month contract, with 2 payouts per contract via e-transfer. They also state they are happy to purchase or consign, so an outright buyout is available - but they publish no buyout terms, so you would have to ask for that figure separately.
orgs.caution: Unsold items not claimed within 7 days of contract expiry are donated to charity by the store - put that date in a diary the day you sign. Email photos, dimensions and condition before turning up with a vanload.

orgs.name: MONA Consignment
orgs.locationsNote: Two locations: 1037 Fort St, downtown Victoria (250 361 9307), taking consignment Tuesday to Saturday 10am-4pm; and 111-2830 Peatt Rd, Langford/Westshore (778 433 6662), Wednesday to Saturday 10am-4pm.
buys: Women's clothing 2-3 years old or newer, in great condition
refuses: Anything stained, holed or excessively worn
Clothing not freshly laundered or dry cleaned
orgs.dealNote: A 3-month consignment contract, with accounts opened with a minimum of 10 pieces. Their site also states that if you would like to be offered a buyout, let them know - so an outright sale is available on request. THE CONSIGNOR PERCENTAGE IS NOT PUBLISHED on their website and we found no figure to quote. It lives in their consignor contract.

At the end of the 3-month contract the items are donated. Their site states items under $100 are not eligible for pickup and are donated to local charities, and anything over $100 must be requested back by email a week before the contract ends.

orgs.name: Old 'N' Gold
orgs.locationsNote: Fixed shop on Fort Street's antique row. Hours on their own site are Monday to Friday 10am-4pm, closed weekends and holidays - the weekend closure catches people out.
buys: Bullion (certified .999 or .9999 fine gold and silver bars or coins, quoted by phone)
orgs.dealNote: CORRECTED AFTER CHECKING THEIR SITE. This is not a buy-only jeweller. Their own page offers four different transactions on the same item: sell for cash, trade, consignment, or collateral-based cash loans on jewellery and precious metals. A collateral-based loan is a pawn loan in substance - borrowing against the item, not selling it. They do not publish what they pay, how an offer is calculated, any interest rate, or any loan term, so every number is quote-by-quote at the counter.
orgs.caution: Be explicit about which of the four transactions you are agreeing to, because a loan and a sale look similar across a counter and only one of them ends with you keeping the item. If you take a collateral loan, ask in writing for the interest, the repayment period and the date the item is forfeited. Separately, scrap gold and silver are priced off weight and purity and no Victoria buyer we checked publishes its rate - if a piece may be worth more as jewellery than as metal, say so before it is quoted as scrap.

orgs.name: Super Chance
orgs.locationsNote: One store in James Bay. Open Monday to Saturday 10am-5pm, Sunday 10am-4pm, statutory holidays 10am-3pm.
buys: Second-hand household goods, per their current accepting list
orgs.dealNote: A consignment store rather than an outright buyer. Their site tells you to send an email with your request and they will reply with a drop-off number and time frame, and that appointments are made for high-end items only. The consignment percentage is not published on their site, and payouts must be requested in advance by phone or email.
orgs.caution: You cannot simply turn up with boxes - the drop-off number and time slot are arranged by email in advance, and there is a separate list of what they are currently accepting. Ask what percentage you keep before agreeing to anything, since the split is not published.

orgs.name: The Bay Street Broker
orgs.locationsNote: One Victoria store. Their contact page publishes two phone numbers (250-381-7296 and 250-383-7467) and hours of Monday to Saturday 9am-6pm. No street address appears anywhere on their site; the services page describes the shop entrance as being at Government and Bay, and a separate pawn entrance off Bay Street with free parking. Phone before you load the car.
buys: Phones (must be wiped to factory settings with all accounts removed, and not connected to a monthly plan)
refuses: Phones still connected to an account or on a monthly plan
Bicycles without the original purchase receipt
orgs.dealNote: Their services page describes three separate transactions, and it matters enormously which one you agree to. (1) A PAWN LOAN, in their words: they loan you cash based on a percent value and hold your item until you return to pay the interest. (2) An OUTRIGHT PURCHASE: they buy the item from you and it is theirs - there is nothing to redeem. (3) CONSIGNMENT: they sell it for you and, in their words, take 25% and taxes. The 25% consignment commission is the only figure the business publishes. It states no interest rate, no loan term and no redemption deadline.
orgs.caution: A pawn is borrowing, not selling. Their own wording is that they hold the item until you return to pay the interest, so if the loan is not repaid the item is not returned. Because this business publishes no interest rate, loan period, or redemption date, ask for the written pawn ticket and read those three things before you hand anything over. Their site states that for pawns every transaction must be done with 2 pieces of ID.

orgs.name: The Turntable
orgs.singleAddress: 107-3 Fan Tan Alley, Victoria, BC V8W 3G9
orgs.locationsNote: One shop in Fan Tan Alley, Chinatown. Open Monday to Sunday 11am-6pm.
orgs.dealNote: Their site says they buy, sell and trade vinyl records, CDs and cassette tapes, and invites you to bring your stuff in to sell, with the option to trade in old albums against their stock. It does not publish how offers are calculated, whether payment is cash or trade credit, or what condition they require - all of that has to be settled at the counter.

orgs.name: Victoria Roadshow
orgs.singleAddress: Paramount Executive Centre, 848 Courtney St. Unit 300, Victoria, BC V8W 1C4
orgs.locationsNote: A downtown office, not a walk-in shop - their site says by appointment only. They also offer complimentary private appointments in your home. Main line (250) 940-3583, 9:00am-4:30pm Monday to Friday, with an after-hours number of (250) 885-6984.
buys: Northwest Coast Indigenous art - masks, weavings, baskets and carvings
orgs.dealNote: Their site says only that after a mutually agreed upon price is accepted for your items, payment will be provided. It does not state the payment method or any percentage of value, so treat every appointment as a negotiation over a single offer.
orgs.caution: This is an appointment-only office, and they will also come to your home. A valuation conducted in your living room is one where you have no comparison quote in the room - if you are bringing out something of real value, get it valued independently first and do not feel obliged to decide on the spot.

orgs.name: Williams Scrap Iron & Metals
orgs.locationsNote: Two yards, and which one you go to changes what you get paid. Main yard: 2690 Munns Rd, Victoria, BC V8T 4K9, 250-479-8335 - take copper, brass and other non-ferrous metal here. Millstream yard: 600 Terlson Ln, Langford, BC V9B 6E2, 250-391-3066 - their site says iron and steel only. Hours Monday to Friday 8am-4:30pm and Saturday 9am-12pm, closed statutory holidays and long weekends; the site says the Millstream yard is open 7 days a week. Family-owned since 1960, now third generation.
buys: Copper #1 (new pipe and bare wire) and Copper #2
orgs.dealNote: Paid by weight and grade. Their site publishes no prices and tells you to call the office to get their current prices, because rates move with the commodity market - so phone the morning you plan to go. They also offer bins and containers and will pick up household or industrial scrap for larger jobs.
orgs.caution: Bring government photo ID. Their site states that, abiding by the BC laws and regulations, they ask customers to have a government ID when bringing in their material. This is not shop policy dressed up as law - see the provincial Act in the regulation note. Separating copper, brass and aluminum out of mixed steel before you arrive is what decides whether you are paid non-ferrous or scrap-steel rates.

metros.name: Saskatoon
metros.localNote: Every business on this list was confirmed by fetching its own website, and every legal statement was confirmed against the Act, the Regulations and the bylaw text. What is published and what is not splits sharply by category. Nobody in Saskatoon publishes what they pay, with one exception. Resurrected Records states \"40-50% of your collection's value\" on its own sell-your-media page. Juniper & Oak publishes a full consignment schedule: 50/50 split, store sets the price, 25% markdowns every 30 days, items under $300 becoming store property after 90 days, and a 12% storage fee for taking something back early. Westgate Books and Peryton Books both publish 50% of their own sell price, in store credit rather than cash. Beyond those four, no pawnshop, scrap yard, gold buyer, salvage yard or buyback store in this city publishes a rate, a percentage or a formula. Anyone quoting one without naming the shop that said it is making it up. The two pawnshops both do loans and outright purchases, and both are silent online about interest, fees and redemption periods. That silence is the single most important fact about them: the cost of borrowing is not knowable from the internet. Scrap and salvage price against commodity markets that move, so no yard publishes rates; Bare Wire will pay in cash or e-transfer and will bring trucks with scales to your address, and supplies bins at no cost. Gold buyers price on metal content - weight and karat - rather than on what a piece is worth intact. Two categories were deliberately left off: gold buyers with no fixed street address operating by appointment only, and pop-up buyers without permanent premises.
metros.regulationNote: All of the following was verified against primary sources fetched directly: The Pawned Property (Recording) Act, c P-4.2 and The Pawned Property (Recording) Regulations, c P-4.2 Reg 1 (both downloaded from the Office of the King's Printer at publications.saskatchewan.ca), and The Business License Bylaw, 2002, Bylaw No. 8075, codified to Bylaw No. 9684, August 31 2020 (downloaded from saskatoon.ca). WHO THE PROVINCIAL RULES BIND. This is the point that decides whether the rest applies to a given shop. Section 2(e) of the Act defines a pawnbroker as \"a person who regularly conducts more than 10 pawn transactions per month\". The Act binds pawnbrokers. It does not impose identification or police-reporting duties on every second-hand dealer in the province, so an ordinary used-electronics shop, record shop, bookshop or jeweller that is not a pawnbroker is outside it. Section 2(g) defines an \"unconditional sale\" as the purchase of an article by a pawnbroker outright - so when a pawnbroker buys something outright, that sale is caught by the Act too, not just the loans. One further condition: section 7(4) says the identification and reporting section applies to a pawnbroker only where the chief of police has given at least 90 days' notice; in Saskatoon, bylaw section 27.7 has required electronic recording and reporting of all pawn transactions since January 1, 2005. IDENTIFICATION - TWO PIECES, ONE WITH A PHOTOGRAPH. Regulation section 4(1) requires a pawnbroker, before a pawn transaction or an unconditional sale, to obtain your name, address, telephone number and date of birth; a description of you including height, weight, gender, hair colour and eye colour; and the identification record numbers from two pieces of identification. One of the two must be one of the following types and only counts if it carries your photograph: a valid driver's licence issued by a Canadian province or territory or a US state; a passport issued by the government of origin; a Certificate of Indian Status Card issued by the Government of Canada; a Certificate of Citizenship Card issued by the Government of Canada; or a Conditional Release Card issued by Correctional Services of Canada. An original birth certificate may be used only if the accompanying second piece carries your photograph. Section 7(2) of the Act sets the consequence, quoted exactly: if a person \"refuses or is unable to provide the information required pursuant to subsection (1), the pawnbroker shall not complete the pawn transaction or unconditional sale.\" SERIAL NUMBERS. Regulation section 5 bars a pawnbroker from taking an article that bears or customarily bears a serial number \"unless the serial number is clearly legible and has not been totally or partially altered, removed or obscured.\" WHAT GETS RECORDED AND WHO SEES IT. Regulation section 4(1)(d) requires a detailed description of the article - manufacturer, year of manufacture, make and model, serial number, identifying marks, any title on the item, the media type for a CD, tape, vinyl record, DVD or VHS, and for jewellery the type, weight, karat, engraving or micro-reference, and the number, type, colour, clarity and shape of each gemstone. Section 4(2) requires the date and time, the price paid or the amount loaned on pawn, and the name of the person conducting the transaction; the dealer must issue you a receipt and retain a hard copy signed by both of you. Regulation section 6 requires the pawnbroker to record this electronically in a format approved by the chief of police immediately after the transaction, provide it to the chief of police as soon as practicable, and file a report at least once each day the shop is open - including a nil report on days with no transactions. A pawn or an outright sale at a pawnshop is therefore an identified, police-reported transaction. EXEMPTIONS - MOST HOUSE-CLEAROUT GOODS ARE OUTSIDE THE ACT. Regulation section 3(f) lists articles the Act does not apply to: second-hand books, magazines, journals, periodicals and other similar printed materials; postage stamps; second-hand infant's, toddler's or children's clothing, shoes, equipment, furniture or safety devices; adult clothing or shoes except leather or fur jackets and coats; second-hand cookware, glassware and eating utensils that do not contain precious metals; waste paper, waste cardboard and waste glass; second-hand furniture; second-hand appliances including refrigerators, freezers, stoves, washers, dryers, dishwashers and garbage compactors; and non-motorized lawn or garden equipment and tools. Section 3 also exempts retail returns for refund, exchange or credit, and acquisitions from a law enforcement agency, from a merchant, retailer or wholesaler with a permanent place of business, from a trustee in bankruptcy, executor, administrator or receiver who shows proof of position, or from a public official acting under judicial authority. SASKATOON'S BYLAW - PART V, PAWNBROKERS. Bylaw 8075 defines a \"pawnshop\" as \"a business wherein more than 10 pawn transactions per month are conducted\" and adopts the Act's definitions of pawnbroker, pawn transaction and unconditional sale. Section 27.2 requires a licence to operate a pawnshop, renewed annually. Section 27.3 bars a pawnshop from being located within 160 metres of another, measured property line to property line, with grandfathering for pawnshops that held a valid licence on October 4, 2004. Section 27.4 sets holding periods: a pawnbroker \"shall hold any property received in a pawn transaction or unconditional sale for at least two consecutive clear business days\", shall not display it for sale for 30 days, and shall not sell it until it has been displayed for sale for at least 15 days after that 30-day period. Section 27.5: a pawnbroker \"shall not engage in a pawn transaction or conditional sale with a person under the age of 18 years.\" Section 27.6: a pawnbroker \"shall not accept personal identification in a pawn transaction\" - your ID document itself cannot be the pawned article. Section 27.7 requires electronic recording and reporting of all pawn transactions under the provincial Act, effective January 1, 2005. PAWNING VERSUS SELLING. Both happen at the same counter and the paperwork looks similar, so the distinction is worth stating plainly. A pawn transaction is defined in the Act as depositing an article with a pawnbroker at interest or in expectation of profit, where it is express or implied that the article may be redeemed or repurchased. You get cash now, the shop holds the item, and you get it back only by repaying the advance plus the lender's charges by the deadline. Miss the deadline and the item is forfeited and sold, and the cash you took is the whole of what you received. An unconditional sale is final on the day. None of the Saskatoon pawnshops whose sites were checked publish interest rates, fees or redemption periods anywhere online, so those figures exist only in the store.
